title: Apollo vs. Instantly: Which should you choose in 2026?
summary: Apollo is a data-first all-in-one; Instantly is cold email infrastructure for volume. A fair 2026 comparison by buyer scenario, with published pricing.
body_text: Apollo is a data-first all-in-one: a large B2B contact database with prospecting, sequencing, and a dialer bundled together. Instantly is cold email infrastructure built for sending volume and deliverability. Choose Apollo when you need leads plus a full sales stack. Choose Instantly when you already have lists and want to send at scale. How Apollo and Instantly compare at a glance Apollo Instantly Category Data-first all-in-one sales platform Cold email sending infrastructure Best for Teams that need contact data and a full outbound stack in one place High-volume senders and agencies that already have lists Standout capability Database of over 230 million contacts with prospecting, sequencing, and dialer Mailbox management, deliverability tooling, and volume sending Data included Yes, native database No native database; you import or buy leads (lead finder with over 450 million leads available) Pricing model Per user/month Per workspace and sending volume Published pricing Free to ~$119/user/month (per its pricing page) ~$47 to $555/month (per its pricing page) Multichannel Email, calls, social media steps Email-centric Apollo vs. Instantly: Which is better? Neither is better in the abstract. They solve different halves of the same problem. Apollo answers "who do I contact and how do I run my whole sales motion." Instantly answers "how do I land thousands of cold emails in the inbox reliably." Many teams that outgrow a single tool end up running both: Apollo for data and pipeline management, Instantly for the raw cold email volume. If you can only pick one, decide what you lack. If you lack a list, Apollo wins because it hands you contacts on day one. If you already have lists and your problem is deliverability and scale, Instantly wins because that is the entire product. What is Apollo best at? Apollo is best at giving a small or mid-sized team a database and a sales stack under one login. Its contact database (Apollo claims over 230 million records) covers prospecting, email verification, sequencing, a built-in dialer, and basic deal tracking. For a founder-led team or a lean sales development representative (SDR) group, this breadth is the draw: you can find a prospect, verify the email, enroll them in a sequence, and log the call without leaving the app. For a data-tool comparison, see Apollo vs. Lusha . The March 2026 Pocus acquisition added product-signal and warm-lead scoring, pushing Apollo further toward intent-aware prospecting. Reported annual recurring revenue (ARR) of around $200M and adoption by more than 600,000 companies (per Apollo) make it one of the most widely used tools in the category. Apollo's honest limit is the scope of its AI, which drafts and suggests while a human still runs the motion. Enterprises frequently treat Apollo as a data layer that feeds a more governed engagement stack instead of a system of record. And the per-seat model means costs climb with headcount. Related: apollo alternatives . What is Instantly best at? Instantly is best at putting large volumes of cold email into inboxes without wrecking your sender reputation. Its core is mailbox provisioning, a shared reputation-building network, deliverability monitoring, and campaign sending built to run many mailboxes at once. Agencies and high-volume outbound teams pick it because sending is the hard part at scale, and Instantly treats that as the product rather than an afterthought. It also ships a lead database (Instantly advertises over 450 million leads) and a light CRM, so you can source and manage inside the same tool. Pricing is transparent, running from roughly $47 to $555/month per its pricing page, which undercuts per-seat data platforms for teams that send a lot from a few accounts. Instantly's honest limit is that it hands you infrastructure, not strategy. You still write the copy, build the targeting, and handle every reply. Its native contact data has poorer coverage than a dedicated data platform's, and its AI assistance is newer than its sending stack. Related: the best Instantly alternatives . How does pricing compare? The pricing models are not directly comparable, which is exactly the point. Apollo prices per seat, from free up to about $119/user/month on its higher published tier, with custom enterprise pricing above that (per its pricing page). Costs scale with the number of reps. Instantly prices per workspace and sending capacity, from roughly $47 to $555/month across its public tiers (per its pricing page). A 3-person agency that sends from 40 mailboxes pays for capacity, not seats, which is usually cheaper for high-volume sending. A 10-rep team that needs data for each rep usually finds Apollo's bundle more economical than buying data separately and paying Instantly for volume it doesn't need. Choose Apollo if... You need contact data and don't want to buy a separate database. You want prospecting, sequencing, and a dialer in one tool. Your team is rep-driven and you value an all-in-one over best-of-breed sending. You care about intent and warm-lead signals (strengthened by the Pocus acquisition). Choose Instantly if... You already have or can source your lists and your bottleneck is deliverability. You send high cold email volume across many mailboxes. You are an agency that runs campaigns for multiple clients. You want transparent, capacity-based pricing rather than per-seat costs. A third path if you'd rather not run either yourself Both tools share the same limitation: each assumes a person drives the motion, building lists, writing copy, testing, and working replies. Apollo hands you data; Instantly hands you sending capacity. Neither runs the outreach itself, which is the job most teams actually want done. If your goal is the outcome rather than the software, an autonomous platform like Artisan is a third path. Its AI business development representative (BDR), Ava, sources leads from a database of over 250 million B2B professionals across over 200 countries, writes and sends personalized campaigns, runs sending placement testing, and handles replies, with over 90% of customers running her autonomously. For a direct comparison, see Artisan vs. Apollo . It is a different model from buying data (Apollo) or buying sending capacity (Instantly): you buy the job done, on usage-based pricing instead of seats or mailbox count. See the AI sales agent overview or the AI BDR primer for how this works. See also Artisan vs. Instantly . Frequently asked questions Can I use Apollo and Instantly together? Yes, and many teams do. A common setup uses Apollo to source and verify contacts, then exports lists into Instantly for high-volume sending across managed mailboxes. Apollo covers data and pipeline; Instantly covers deliverability and scale. The trade-off is two subscriptions and two systems to reconcile. Does Instantly include a contact database? Instantly advertises a lead finder with over 450 million leads and a light CRM, so you can source inside the tool. In practice, teams that need deep, accurate firmographic and technographic data often still pair it with a dedicated data provider. Instantly's strength is sending, not data depth. Which has better deliverability? Instantly is built around deliverability: mailbox provisioning, a shared reputation-building network, placement monitoring, and dynamic send limits. Apollo sends too, but deliverability infrastructure is a smaller part of a much broader product. For pure high-volume cold email, Instantly is the more specialized tool. Is Apollo good for enterprise? Apollo scales to larger teams, but enterprises often adopt it as a data and prospecting layer rather than their governed engagement system of record. Its AI is assistive, and per-seat pricing grows with headcount. Evaluate it against dedicated enterprise sequencing and data platforms if governance and audit trails are priorities. For a sequencing comparison, see Apollo vs. Outreach . Which is cheaper? It depends on shape. For a few people sending high volume, Instantly's capacity-based pricing (about $47 to $555/month per its pricing page) is usually cheaper. For a larger rep team that would otherwise buy data separately, Apollo's bundled per-seat model (free to roughly $119/user/month) often wins. Map your seat count against your sending volume. Does either of them write and send campaigns automatically? No. Both automate mechanics like enrollment, sending, and follow-up timing, but a person still defines targeting, writes the messaging, and works the replies. Fully autonomous prospecting, where an AI owns the end-to-end BDR job, is a separate category of tool. Is there an alternative to both Apollo and Instantly? Yes. If you would rather not stitch a data tool to a sending tool and still run the motion yourself, an autonomous platform is the alternative. Artisan's AI BDR, Ava, combines a database of over 250 million B2B professionals with campaign writing, sending, and reply handling in one system on usage-based pricing , so the sourcing and the sending live together and the AI runs them. It is a different purchase from buying data or buying capacity; see Artisan's AI sales agent for detail. For a wider view of the category, see our roundup of the best cold email tools , or compare approaches on the Artisan homepage . See also Apollo vs. Lemlist . title: Robinhood Ventures Fund II invests in Didit
summary: Didit joins the Robinhood Ventures Fund II portfolio — Robinhood's NYSE-listed fund of ~80 private startups. The fund's structure, allocation, and what's next.
body_text: Back to blog Blog · August 6, 2026 Robinhood Ventures Fund II invests in Didit Didit is part of the portfolio of Robinhood Ventures Fund II (NYSE: RVII), Robinhood's new fund that gives retail investors access to private startups. Here is what the fund is, how it works, and what it means for Didit. By Didit · August 6, 2026 · Updated Aug 6, 2026 Some news we are proud to share: Robinhood Ventures Fund II has invested in Didit. Didit is part of the portfolio that the fund brings to the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker RVII . For a company whose whole reason to exist is opening up infrastructure that used to be reserved for large enterprises, being part of a fund built to open up venture capital itself feels exactly right. What Robinhood Ventures Fund II is Venture capital has historically been closed to almost everyone. If you were not a fund LP or an accredited insider, your first chance to own a piece of a great company came at its IPO — often a decade after the value was created. Robinhood Ventures Fund II is Robinhood's answer to that. It is a closed-end fund (a business development company, regulated under the Investment Company Act of 1940) managed by Robinhood Ventures, an SEC-registered investment adviser and subsidiary of Robinhood Markets. Instead of a private LP base, the fund lists a fixed number of shares on the New York Stock Exchange, where anyone with a brokerage account can buy them. "Retail investors no longer have to wait until a company's IPO to be part of an early growth journey," is how Sarah Pinto, Head of Robinhood Ventures, put it at the fund's announcement. The mechanics, briefly: Ticker RVII (NYSE) Structure Closed-end fund / BDC Expected IPO August 13, 2026, at an expected $25.00 per share Share request window Open through August 12, 2026 Portfolio ~80 private companies at IPO, with more added over time Adviser Robinhood Ventures (Robinhood Markets subsidiary) Fees 2.00% annual management fee, 20% incentive fee on realized gains Transparency Holdings published quarterly in the Robinhood app and in SEC filings Inside the portfolio The fund's thesis leans on Y Combinator. RVII invests primarily in early- and growth-stage companies that went through the Y Combinator accelerator or were founded by YC alumni — a pool of more than 5,000 companies funded since 2005, together worth over $1.3 trillion. "Y Combinator has one of the strongest track records in venture," said Rich Aberman, the fund's portfolio manager. (Y Combinator itself does not sponsor or endorse the fund.) Didit fits that thesis from both sides: we are a Y Combinator-backed company, and we sell the kind of infrastructure the rest of the portfolio increasingly depends on. The fund is deliberately diversified. As of the July 15, 2026 snapshot published by Robinhood, the sector allocation looks like this: Sector Allocation Technology 64.3% Industrials 9.0% Financial services 7.8% Healthcare 6.7% Consumer cyclical 2.2% Energy 1.1% Communication services 1.1% Cash and equivalents 7.4% Position sizing is deliberately even, too: outside a couple of anchor positions, most holdings — Didit among them — sit at roughly 1% of the fund each. The exact weights will be published with each quarterly disclosure. Why identity infrastructure Every company in a portfolio like this one eventually meets the same problem: proving who is on the other side of the screen. Fraud is now industrialized — deepfakes, injection attacks, synthetic identities — and regulation is expanding at the same pace. Didit is infrastructure for identity and fraud. Four product lines — User Verification, Business Verification, Transaction Monitoring, and Wallet Screening — behind one API, one workflow builder, and one dashboard: 2,000+ companies run verification on Didit today. Coverage for 220+ countries and territories and 14,000+ document types , in 48+ languages. Sub-2-second p99 decisions, with 200+ real-time AI fraud signals including deepfake and injection detection. Screening against 1,300+ AML watchlists , with full KYC from $0.33 per verification and 500 free verifications every month. That is the company Robinhood Ventures chose to put in the portfolio, and we intend to keep earning the spot. What changes for Didit customers Nothing in your integration, and nothing in our pricing. Didit remains an independent company; Robinhood Ventures joins backers including Y Combinator on our cap table. What the investment does change is trajectory: more capital behind the roadmap, and a very public incentive to keep shipping — because from August 13 onward, anyone who believes in what we are building can literally own a piece of the journey through RVII. The fine print A transparency note, because we sell to compliance teams and they would expect nothing less: this post is an announcement, not investment advice, and not an offer to sell securities. Didit is not selling shares to the public — RVII is a fund managed by Robinhood Ventures that holds a stake in Didit alongside ~80 other companies. Early-stage investing is risky and illiquid; anyone considering RVII should read the fund's prospectus and risk disclosures on robinhood.com before requesting shares. To Sarah, Rich, and the Robinhood Ventures team: thank you for the trust. To everyone building on Didit: this one is as much yours as ours. title: Make a Witchy New England Escape That’s Full of Fall Magic
summary: Plan a magical New England escape that blends coastal beauty, storybook villages, dark academia vibes and centuries‑old history.
body_text: Listen to this article 0:00 Follow winding roads through bewitching landscapes, discover enchanting hidden bookshops and uncover captivating Autumn charm in New England Plan a magical New England escape that blends coastal beauty, storybook villages, dark academia vibes and centuries-old history during the region's most hypnotizing season. From Boston to Providence and beyond, explore witchy autumn experiences ranging from ghost tours and ghoulish graveyards to cozy bookstores, misty harbors, covered bridges and colorful leaf-peeping drives. Stay in alluring Hilton properties throughout Massachusetts, Rhode Island, Connecticut and Maine, each steeped in their own stories, for a fall getaway filled with fantasy, folklore and seasonal charm. There’s something so magical about autumn in New England. The crisp air, colorful foliage and centuries-old homes give an enchanting feel to an already charming corner of the world. A trip here during spooky season is a vibe, offering cobblestone streets with eerily quiet corners, cozy bookshops filled with spellbinding tomes and winding roads through misty landscapes that make for the prime setting for ghost stories and witchy tales. While Salem is a natural draw for those seeking a haunting hangout, some of New England’s most hypnotizing fall experiences can be found lurking elsewhere, in places where folklore, history, natural beauty and a touch of mystery create the perfect backdrop for a magical, mischievous getaway. Boston, Massachusetts is a Storied Setting Steeped in History Beacon Hill Neighborhood in Boston, Massachusetts - Photo Credit: haveseen/Shutterstock Every bewitching adventure needs a launching point, and Boston is the perfect place to begin. As one of America’s oldest cities, Boston offers centuries of history with an undeniable air of mystique. Here, colonial-era graveyards provide an unnerving backdrop for ghost tours and deep dives into local legends. title: Microsoft named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Cloud-Native Application Platforms
summary: Microsoft was named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Cloud-Native Application Platforms, helping organizations modernize applications, build AI agents, and scale securely.
body_text: Microsoft has been named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Cloud-Native Application Platforms , which we believe recognizes the platforms organizations rely on to build, deploy, and operate cloud-native applications at scale. This is our third consecutive year positioned as a Leader in this report. Read the report We are proud of this recognition. More importantly, we believe it reflects a shift we see across industries. Cloud-native application platforms are no longer where organizations build and run modern applications. They are becoming the foundation for AI transformation. The challenge is not a shortage of AI ideas. It is turning those ideas into production systems that can connect to existing applications and data, perform reliably at global scale, and meet the security and governance standards the business already expects. That requires more than a collection of application services. It requires a platform that brings application modernization, AI innovation, operations, and security together. Microsoft’s cloud-native application platform is designed around that reality. Azure App Service provides a managed foundation for enterprise web applications and modernization. Container Apps runs cloud-native applications, APIs, AI inferencing, and agents without requiring teams to manage infrastructure. Azure Functions provides event-driven execution and integration, while API Management governs APIs, models, and agent tools through a consistent policy layer. Together with Microsoft Foundry , GitHub Copilot , and the shared Azure foundation for identity, networking, observability, and security, these capabilities give organizations one platform for what they already run and what they build next. Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ graphic for Cloud-Native Applications Platform 2026 Build AI apps and agents faster Microsoft brings the application runtime and AI toolchain together so developers can build with the model, framework, and architecture that fits the job. Microsoft Foundry provides the models, agent tooling, evaluation, tracing, and safety capabilities needed to take AI systems into production. GitHub Copilot helps developers move faster across the development lifecycle. Azure’s application platform provides the managed runtime, event-driven execution, integration, and API capabilities to turn those systems into applications people can rely on. This is where platform capabilities matter. Developers can deploy a container directly to a production endpoint with Azure Container Apps Express , and use Azure Functions to expose existing business logic through the Model Context Protocol. More than 1,400 connectors help agents act across enterprise systems without requiring developers to rebuild authentication, retries, and integration logic for every connection. Azure Container Apps Sandboxes provide the isolated compute that agent platforms run on. The same primitive runs the agent itself, hosts its tools and MCP servers, and executes the code it generates, each in its own microVM, hardware-isolated boundary, with state that survives when the agent pauses. It is the compute layer behind Foundry Agent Service and is available to customers building and operating their own agent platforms on Azure. The result is a shorter path from an AI idea to a governed application or agent that can deliver on your business goals. Modernize applications regardless of architecture AI transformation starts with the application estate organizations already have, not a blank slate. Azure gives teams a practical path to modernize at their own pace. They can move established applications to fully managed Platform as a Service (PaaS) services, containerize where it makes sense, adopt event-driven patterns incrementally, and extend existing business logic so it can participate in AI-powered experiences. App Service Managed Instance helps organizations move complex Windows and .NET applications without requiring a rewrite, while GitHub Copilot app modernization accelerates assessment and remediation. Once modernized, those applications can connect to the same data, AI services, APIs, identity controls, and operational practices as new cloud-native applications. This flexibility protects the value already in the application estate while creating a foundation for continuous innovation. Organizations do not have to choose between modernizing the core and building for the AI era. The platform makes those efforts part of the same strategy. Secure, govern, and simplify operations AI applications raise the operational bar. Agents can call APIs, execute generated code, and interact with sensitive systems at a speed and volume that traditional controls were not designed to manage. Security, governance, and observability cannot be added after deployment. They need to be part of the platform. Azure provides shared identity, networking, policy, and security controls across the application estate. Azure API Management extends that consistency to APIs, MCP servers, and model endpoints. Its AI gateway capabilities help teams authenticate access, enforce token limits and quotas, balance traffic across models, apply semantic caching, and monitor how AI services are consumed. Azure Container Apps Sandboxes add hardware-level isolation for agent-generated or untrusted code, while confidential computing and Microsoft Defender strengthen protection for sensitive workloads. Operations also need to keep pace with development. Azure combines global reach with managed scaling across web apps, containers, functions, and APIs. Built-in load balancing, zone redundancy, deployment controls, and integrated observability help teams maintain performance as usage grows. Azure Monitor and Application Insights give teams end-to-end visibility across applications and AI workloads. Azure SRE Agent brings agentic operations into that environment by helping teams investigate incidents, identify root causes, and take auditable remediation actions. Together with GitHub Copilot , these capabilities create a secure and reliable path across the application lifecycle, from development to production operations. Customer momentum across the platform Across banking, retail, healthcare, manufacturing, IT, and other industries, organizations are running their most critical applications and their newest AI workloads on the same Azure foundation. A clean cloud architecture is a prerequisite for AI. You can’t build on top of a weak foundation. Mike Gibson, Chief Technology Officer, Planet DDS Planet DDS built that foundation on Azure. It modernized its platform on Azure App Service and cut provisioning time from six weeks to one day, which gives its teams room to invest in the product rather than the plumbing. Replit and Microsoft Azure now put enterprise software building in reach of every Hexaware employee, extending development beyond the people who write code for a living. That same platform is already running AI in production. Commerzbank runs its agentic AI architecture on Azure Container Apps , where its Ava assistant handles more than 30,000 customer conversations each month and resolves 75% of them autonomously. Ghassan Aboud Group built its Ragin AI platform on Azure Container Apps to deliver agentic customer experiences across its businesses. Levi Strauss and Co. uses Microsoft Foundry to simplify everyday work and accelerate decision-making. These are not experiments running alongside the business. They are AI systems operating inside it. Taken together, these stories describe one platform doing several jobs at once. It carries existing applications forward, runs new AI and agentic workloads in production, and gives organizations a common foundation to operate both with confidence. We believe the next generation of applications will be cloud-native, AI-powered, and deeply connected to the systems organizations already rely on. In our view, Microsoft’s position as a Leader for the third consecutive year reinforces our commitment to giving every organization one secure, scalable platform to modernize what it has and build what comes next. Get started Wherever you are in your journey, there is a place to begin today. Building AI apps and agents . Start on Azure Container Apps to build your agentic applications with built-in enterprise security and ultra-fast scale. Modernizing existing applications . Bring Windows and .NET workloads forward with App Service Managed Instance , and use GitHub Copilot app modernization to accelerate assessment and remediation. Running event-driven and API-centric workloads . Build with Azure Functions and manage your APIs, MCP servers, and model endpoints through Azure API Management. Operating with confidence . Add Azure SRE Agent and Azure Monitor to bring agentic operations and end-to-end observability to what you already run. title: Migrate from Intercom to Zendesk Step-by-Step Intercom Migration Guide
summary: Migrate from Intercom to Zendesk with this step-by-step guide covering data migration, setup, testing, cutover, and optimization.
body_text: Here is what most teams get wrong about help desk migrations: they focus on moving data when the real challenge is preserving operational continuity. Intercom conversations do not map cleanly to Zendesk tickets. Automation rules built over years disappear during transfer. Agent workflows that took months to optimize must be rebuilt from scratch. The technical process of moving records from one platform to another is well-documented. But the hidden costs of migration, including lost productivity during transition, the weeks spent rebuilding automations, and the training overhead for teams learning new interfaces, often exceed the direct migration expenses. This is where Slack-native ticketing offers a fundamentally different approach. Instead of migrating between traditional help desk platforms, teams can adopt conversational ticketing that works directly within the tools employees already use. The question is not just how to migrate from Intercom to Zendesk, but whether a traditional migration makes sense when newer architectures eliminate the underlying friction. Key Takeaways Intercom to Zendesk migrations may take one to several weeks end-to-end when planning, data transfer, workflow rebuilding, validation, and agent training are included. The automated transfer itself often finishes within 24 to 48 hours , although the total project timeline varies by scope and complexity. Conversation-to-ticket mapping is the critical technical challenge because Intercom organizes support around rolling conversations while Zendesk uses a ticket-centric model. Running a free demo migration with a small set of representative tickets before committing catches threading issues that would otherwise require manual cleanup across thousands of tickets. Migration services automate data transfer but workflows must be rebuilt manually. Saved replies, automation rules, and bot logic do not transfer automatically and can represent a substantial part of the migration project because they must be reviewed, redesigned, and recreated in Zendesk. Slack-native alternatives can reduce some migration and adoption complexity by turning workplace conversations into structured tickets without requiring employees to learn a separate request interface. Historical data, integrations, workflows, and governance requirements may still need to be configured or migrated. Why Consider Migrating Your Help Desk Software? Help desk migrations typically stem from specific operational pain points rather than general dissatisfaction. Understanding actual drivers helps determine whether Zendesk addresses them or whether alternative approaches might serve better. Common migration triggers include: Unpredictable billing models: Per-resolution AI charges or tiered seat pricing can create monthly cost fluctuations that complicate budgeting. Feature limitations: Reporting, routing, or automation capabilities may not scale with team complexity. Integration gaps: Native connections to CRMs, HR systems, or development tools may require workarounds. User experience friction: Agents may spend excessive time context-switching between platforms. Vendor uncertainty: Acquisitions, leadership changes, or product roadmap shifts may affect long-term planning. The decision to migrate should be grounded in documented operational problems. Teams migrating primarily for cost savings should calculate implementation expenses, workflow rebuilding, training time, and short-term productivity changes before estimating first-year savings. Teams migrating for specific capability gaps, such as better analytics, multichannel routing, or enterprise security features, typically see faster returns. Evaluating Your Current Help Desk Needs Before committing to any migration, audit the current state: Document which Intercom features the team actually uses versus which sit dormant. Identify automation rules that would need rebuilding and calculate the hours required. Survey agents about pain points to distinguish platform limitations from training gaps. This audit often reveals that the problem is not the platform itself but how teams interact with it. If agents complain about too many tools, migrating to another external platform does not solve the underlying context-switching problem that Slack-native solutions address directly. Intercom Alternatives Zendesk represents one migration path, but the help desk landscape has evolved significantly. Understanding different architectural approaches helps teams select platforms aligned with how they actually work. Traditional ticketing platforms: Platforms like Zendesk organize work around discrete tickets with defined lifecycles. Requests enter through various channels, become tickets, move through status workflows, and close. This model works well for high-volume, transactional support but can feel rigid for collaborative internal teams. Conversational platforms: Platforms like Intercom blur the line between chat and ticketing. Conversations flow naturally but can lack the structure needed for SLA tracking, complex routing, and cross-team handoffs. Slack-native platforms: Instead of pulling conversations into an external system, these solutions add ticketing structure directly within Slack. Employees submit requests in channels they already use, teams manage work without opening separate applications, and automation happens behind the scenes while conversations remain natural. The Rise of Conversational AI Helpdesks The newest generation of help desk platforms builds AI into the foundation rather than bolting it on afterward. This architectural difference matters because purpose-built AI agents can: Automatically resolve a meaningful share of routine internal tickets. Understand conversational context from the start. Reference connected knowledge and trigger actions within employee workflows. One Unthread customer reports that the platform automatically resolves about 40% of tickets across its teams when designed for conversational workflows from the start. Traditional platforms adding AI features retrofit capabilities onto ticket-centric architectures. The result often feels disconnected, with AI suggestions appearing in sidebars rather than naturally within conversations. Native AI architectures understand context, reference knowledge bases, and take actions within the same interface where conversations happen. Zendesk vs. Unthread: A Modern Approach to Internal Support Needs Zendesk has served as a help desk platform for over a decade. Its comprehensive feature set handles virtually any support scenario. But comprehensiveness comes with complexity, and complexity creates friction for teams seeking simpler solutions. Key differences include: Ticket creation: Zendesk relies on manual entry or integrations, while Unthread creates tickets automatically from Slack conversations. Agent interface: Zendesk uses a dedicated web application, whereas Unthread works natively within the Slack workspace. AI capabilities: Zendesk offers AI as add-on features, while Unthread offers purpose-built AI agents . Setup complexity: Zendesk typically requires weeks of configuration, while Unthread can reach the first ticket within hours. Workflow changes: Zendesk requires admin console work, while Unthread supports natural language or visual builders. For teams already living in Slack, migrating to Zendesk introduces a new application that agents must learn, monitor, and context-switch into. Unthread eliminates this overhead by turning existing Slack channels into structured help desks. A channel like #it-help becomes a complete ticketing system with routing, SLAs, and automation without requiring employees to change how they request help. The Power of Purpose-Built AI Agents Unthread's AI does not just suggest responses. It automatically resolves tickets by: Referencing knowledge base articles. Understanding request intent. Drafting accurate responses. Triggering appropriate internal workflows. This agentic approach means routine requests for password resets, software access, or policy questions resolve without human intervention. The platform also supports bring-your-own-LLM through MCP integration. Organizations can choose supported language models, use their own model credentials, and connect existing AI agents through Unthread's model-agnostic and MCP-based integrations, subject to their selected provider and deployment architecture. This flexibility matters particularly for HR service desks handling confidential employee matters. Planning Your Data Migration If Zendesk remains the chosen destination, thorough planning prevents the most common migration failures. The gap between a smooth transition and months of cleanup typically comes down to preparation quality. Defining Your Migration Scope Not all historical data deserves migration. Moving years of stale conversations and duplicate contacts creates a cluttered Zendesk instance that hampers rather than helps agents. Most teams should migrate: Open tickets currently requiring attention. Recent closed tickets from the past 12 to 24 months for context. Active employee and contractor profiles with open requests or relevant service history. Knowledge base articles that remain accurate and useful. Custom field data essential for routing and reporting. Archive rather than migrate old conversations that agents will never reference. This reduces migration costs, speeds transfer times, and creates a cleaner starting point. Creating a Data Mapping Strategy Intercom and Zendesk use different data models: Intercom conversations become Zendesk tickets. Intercom contacts become Zendesk end users. Intercom companies become Zendesk organizations. Custom data attributes require manual mapping to Zendesk custom fields. Critical mapping decisions include: Status mapping: Intercom open, closed, and snoozed states must map to Zendesk new, open, pending, solved, and closed statuses. Lead distinction: Intercom separates Users and Leads while Zendesk treats both as Users. Add a "lead" tag during migration to preserve this distinction. Dropdown fields: Create all dropdown options in Zendesk before migration. Exact option values must match or the field population fails. Step-by-Step Intercom Migration to Zendesk The actual migration process follows a predictable sequence. Understanding each phase helps teams allocate resources appropriately and avoid common pitfalls. Pre-Migration Checklist Week 1 to 2: Environment Preparation Create a Zendesk account. Select a Zendesk plan that includes the routing, automation, reporting, SLA, knowledge base, and channel capabilities required by internal support workflows. Manually create all agents matching Intercom admin roles. Set up groups and teams mirroring the current structure. Recreate Intercom custom attributes as Zendesk custom fields. Export saved replies and workflow documentation for rebuild reference. Days 1 to 3: Migration Tool Setup Sign up for a migration service. Connect both platforms via OAuth or API key. Configure field mappings, verifying auto-mapped fields and manually mapping custom attributes. Set migration options for Delta sync, attachment handling, and tags. Executing the Migration Safely Demo Migration (Day 3 to 4) Run the free demo using representative tickets, including: Multi-threaded conversations. Attachments and inline images. Custom field values. Multiple agent assignments. Validate results thoroughly. Skipping demo validation leads to thousands of mis-mapped tickets that require manual correction. Full Migration (Day 5 to 7) Schedule during low-volume periods. The migration runs in the background while agents continue working in Intercom normally. After completion, run Delta sync to capture conversations created during the transfer window. Post-Migration Verification (Day 8 to 10) Complete the following checks: Compare record counts between systems. Spot-check 50 to 100 random tickets across date ranges. Verify attachments load correctly. Confirm custom fields populate as expected. Validate conversation threads and required field mappings. Resolve any material migration errors before cutover. Do not proceed with cutover until record counts reconcile, required fields are populated correctly, attachments and conversation threads have been validated, and any material migration errors have been resolved. Optimizing Your Zendesk Support After Migration Data in Zendesk is just the starting point. Operational parity requires rebuilding the workflows, automations, and integrations that made the previous setup functional. Fine-tuning Workflows and Automations Elements requiring manual recreation include: Saved replies: Convert these into Zendesk macros by copying them from the export. Intercom workflows: Rebuild them as Zendesk triggers, automations, and routing rules. Bot logic: Recreate it using Zendesk AI tools or third-party layers. Channel connections: Reconfigure email, chat, and social channels. Budget 2 to 5 days for this phase depending on automation complexity. Workflow rebuilding can consume a substantial share of the project, particularly when the existing Intercom setup contains complex routing, automations, segments, or bot logic. Measuring Success and Iterating Track key metrics immediately after go-live to identify gaps: First response time compared to the Intercom baseline. Ticket routing accuracy for automated assignments. Agent productivity during the learning curve. Employee satisfaction scores during transition. For teams seeking advanced analytics without Zendesk's complexity, Unthread's AI analytics provides real-time tracking of support volume, SLA breaches, and recurring issue patterns with automatic grouping and trend analysis. Enhancing Support with AI The help desk category has shifted from tool-centric to outcome-centric. Teams no longer evaluate platforms on feature checklists but on measurable results: tickets resolved, time saved, and employee satisfaction improved. The Future of Support: Agentic AI Traditional automation follows rigid rules. If a ticket contains "password reset," then assign it to the IT team. This approach handles known scenarios but fails on novel requests. Agentic AI can: Understand the employee's intent. Reference conversation and employee context. Determine the appropriate action. Initiate workflows or escalate based on urgency. When an employee asks, "I can't get into my email and I have a presentation in 30 minutes," a purpose-built AI agent recognizes the urgency, initiates password reset procedures, and escalates if needed, all within the conversation. Unthread's agentic platform demonstrates this difference. Rather than deflecting tickets to knowledge base articles, the AI resolves them directly. It triggers workflows, updates external tools, and hands off to humans only when genuinely needed. One Unthread customer highlights that approximately 40% of incoming tickets are automatically resolved across its teams. Integrating Advanced AI Whether choosing Zendesk, Unthread, or another platform, evaluate its AI capabilities based on: Resolution quality: Measure completed outcomes, not just deflection volume. Sending users to articles is not resolution. Context awareness: Determine whether the AI uses conversation history and employee details. Action capability: Confirm whether it can actually resolve issues rather than only suggest solutions. Learning capacity: Evaluate whether it improves from resolved tickets over time. Unthread's self-learning knowledge base exemplifies this progression. The system: Detects repeat questions from ticket history and generates draft help articles automatically. Flags outdated documentation when ticket patterns indicate information gaps. Syncs articles from existing sources like Google Drive and Notion. Keeps knowledge accessible within Slack conversations. Seamless Communication Most internal teams already communicate in Slack. Adding Zendesk creates another destination agents must monitor, another interface to learn, and another place where context gets lost. Leveraging Slack for Internal Collaboration The two approaches use Slack differently: Zendesk integrations: Notify agents of new tickets or allow status updates from Slack, treating Slack primarily as a notification channel. Native Slack ticketing: Places the ticket directly within Slack so agents can manage work without leaving their primary communication tool. Native Slack ticketing inverts the traditional relationship. Employees submit requests in familiar channels, and the entire conversation, from initial request through resolution, happens where work already occurs. This architectural difference matters most for internal support teams. IT, HR, and operations groups supporting employees benefit from removing the friction of external ticketing portals. An employee asking a benefits question in #hr-help gets a structured ticket experience without knowing or caring that ticketing exists. Building a Connected Ecosystem Regardless of platform choice, integration depth determines operational efficiency. Unthread offers 100+ native integrations including Jira, Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Okta, along with API and webhook options for connecting additional internal systems. Connected workflows can support scenarios such as: A new hire request creating accounts on multiple platforms. A security alert routing to on-call engineers. A procurement approval moving through finance. An internal request updating the relevant system automatically. The automation builder supports three creation methods: Natural language descriptions converted to working automations. Visual drag-and-drop interfaces. Custom code for advanced logic. This flexibility means admins can adjust workflows as needs change without requiring engineering resources. Measuring Success Migration success is not about completing data transfer. It is about achieving the operational improvements that motivated the change. Defining Your KPIs Essential metrics to track include: SLA compliance: Response and resolution time performance. First contact resolution rate: An indicator of effective routing and agent empowerment. Ticket volume by category: A way to reveal automation opportunities. Agent productivity: Tickets per hour and handle time. AI deflection rate: The percentage resolved without human intervention. Employee satisfaction: CSAT and NPS survey results. Utilizing Analytics Raw metrics require context to drive decisions. Knowing that ticket volume increased 20% matters less than understanding that HR policy questions spiked following a benefits change announcement. Unthread's analytics includes: Automatic trend analysis and incident detection. Identification of recurring issues. Suggested documentation gaps. Alerts for SLA breaches before they cascade. Custom dashboard exports to BI tools like Looker and Tableau. The best internal help desk helps teams identify recurring issues, automate repetitive work, and reduce avoidable ticket volume over time. Streamline Internal Support with Unthread's Slack-Native Platform For teams evaluating migration paths, Unthread offers a fundamentally different approach to internal support delivery. Instead of pulling employees out of Slack into a separate ticketing interface, Unthread converts existing Slack channels into fully structured help desks. Employees request help exactly where they already work, while support teams gain enterprise-grade ticketing, routing, SLA tracking, and automation behind the scenes. Key capabilities include: Unthread's purpose-built AI , which automatically resolves routine requests by understanding intent, referencing connected knowledge bases, and taking action within the conversation. 100+ native integrations that connect IT systems, HR platforms, and development tools so workflows trigger automatically across the internal tech stack. Real-time analytics that surface recurring issues, flag documentation gaps, and track SLA performance without requiring manual report building. This architecture eliminates the friction of traditional migrations. No separate portal to train employees on. No context-switching for agents. No rebuilding workflows in unfamiliar admin consoles. For internal IT, HR, and operations teams, Unthread delivers the structure of enterprise ticketing with the simplicity of Slack conversations. Frequently Asked Questions What data does not transfer automatically during migration? Several critical elements require manual recreation after migration. Saved replies must be copied into Zendesk as macros individually. Workflow automations and routing rules do not transfer and must be rebuilt using Zendesk's trigger and automation tools. Bot logic including Fin configurations requires complete reconstruction. Email routing, chat widgets, and social channel connections need reconfiguration in the new platform. Custom reports and dashboards must be recreated in Zendesk Explore. Plan dedicated time for this rebuild work, with the required effort depending on the number and complexity of existing workflows. How is the Lead versus User distinction handled when migrating? Intercom maintains separate classifications for Leads (potential contacts) and Users (existing contacts), but Zendesk treats both as end users without native distinction. The recommended approach is to add a tag or custom field during migration that preserves this classification. Configure the migration service to apply this tag to all Intercom Lead records. Post-migration, filtering, reporting, and routing tickets based on this tag maintains workflow continuity. What happens to conversations created during the migration window? Active migrations typically run for 24 to 48 hours depending on data volume. During this period, teams continue working in Intercom normally. Migration services include Delta sync functionality that captures all new and updated conversations created during the transfer window. After the main migration completes, run Delta sync to pull these in-flight conversations into Zendesk. This reduces the risk of gaps in ticket history by capturing conversations created or updated during the main transfer window. Should all historical conversations be migrated or only recent ones? Most teams benefit from selective migration rather than complete historical transfer. Migrating years of old conversations creates a cluttered instance, increases migration costs, and extends transfer times without proportional value. The typical recommendation is migrating all open tickets, closed tickets from the past 12 to 24 months, and active employee profiles. Older conversations can be exported to archival storage for compliance purposes without cluttering the production environment. Define scope based on how often agents actually reference historical conversations. Can the migration be tested before committing? Yes, and this step should not be skipped. Some migration services offer free demos using a limited set of real tickets and knowledge base articles that let field mapping, conversation threading, and attachment handling be validated before paying for full migration. Select complex test cases including multi-threaded conversations, tickets with attachments, and records with custom field values. Validate results thoroughly in Zendesk before proceeding. Issues identified in the demo prevent hours of post-migration cleanup across thousands of records.

title: Pulse is now on Claude
summary: Pulse is now a connector in Claude's directory. Point Claude at any document by URL and get back clean, structured data without leaving the conversation. | Pulse AI
body_text: Pulse is now available as a connector in Claude's directory. Point Claude at any document and get back clean, structured data, without leaving the conversation. What the Pulse connector does Once connected, Claude can call six things directly through Pulse: Extract. Point Claude at any document by URL and get back clean markdown, tables, and JSON. No copy-paste, no manual transcription. Extract tables. Pull tables out of a completed extraction, including merge-across-pages for tables that span multiple sheets, and chart-to-table conversion for documents where the data only exists as a chart image. Split document. Break a long, completed extraction into topic-based page ranges you define, useful for pulling just the relevant section out of a large filing or spec sheet. Apply schema. Run a JSON schema against a completed extraction (or a split of one) and get back structured field values, with citations back to where each value came from in the source document. You can write the schema yourself or have Pulse generate one. Batch extract. Run extraction across many files at once, either from a list of URLs or an S3 prefix, with results written back to S3 or a local path. Run pipeline. Execute a saved, multi-step extraction pipeline against a file. Pipelines themselves are authored in the Pulse dashboard; the connector runs the ones you've already built. Why this matters Every one of Pulse's six capabilities maps to a real step in the same underlying workflow: get structured data out of a document, shape that data to match the fields you actually care about, and do it across one file or thousands. Making that available inside Claude means a team's data extraction step no longer has to be a detour through a separate dashboard. It can happen in the same conversation where someone is already asking the question. Get started Open Claude and go to the Connectors directory ( LINK HERE ). Search for Pulse and connect your account, this is an OAuth flow through Pulse, no manual API keys. Point Claude at a document by URL and ask it to extract, apply a schema, or run a saved pipeline. Approve each tool call the first time; after that you can choose to always allow it.

title: Liberty Global Tech Ventures Invests in AI Video Company, Higgsfield
summary: Liberty Global Tech Ventures, the technology investment arm of Liberty Global, today announced an investment in Higgsfield.
body_text: Liberty Global Tech Ventures, the technology investment arm of Liberty Global, today announced an investment in Higgsfield, an AI video and image creation platform for creators, brands, agencies and studios. Higgsfield has grown rapidly to $700m annualised revenue since launching its browser-based video platform in 2025. The company powers visual production for 390 of the Fortune 500 companies and is used by more than 30 million users across 238 countries and territories. Liberty Global joins a select group of institutional investors – including DST Global, Goldman Sachs, Menlo Ventures, and Accel – alongside strategic investors like Intel in the $400m funding round. Liberty Global’s selection reflects the strategic value it brings through its global technology footprint and experience scaling digital platforms. Global spending on digital advertising is forecast to top $1.1t by 2030 , with video and image creation, a crucial part of the ecosystem, set to be reshaped by AI. Higgsfield’s enterprise customer base spans broadcasting, financial services, advertising and retail with these users driving more than 20 million content generations per month, a 42-fold increase following the rollout of its Supercomputer Agent in May 2026. Liberty Global’s AI Investment Strategy Liberty Global Tech Ventures is part of Liberty Growth, Liberty Global’s investment portfolio focused on scalable technology, media, sports, services and infrastructure. The Tech Ventures team invests in category-defining AI and technology businesses which operate in large markets with management teams who have proven ability to launch and commercialise products. Ankur Prakash, Partner at Liberty Global Tech Ventures, said: “This is a continuation of our strategy of investing in the best technology and people in sectors that are being disrupted by AI technology. Higgsfield is the undoubted market leader in AI video and image creation and already boast some of the world’s largest brands and creative agencies amongst its clientele.”

title: Novavax Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Operational Highlights
summary: Reported total revenue of $57 million for the second quarter of 2026 and raised full-year 2026 Revenue Framework Improved GAAP Combined R&D and SG&A expense guidance by $10 million at mid-point...
body_text: Investors Newsroom Blog People & Culture Science & Technology Overview Matrix-M® Adjuvant Technology Platform Publications Products & Pipeline Products Pipeline Disease Areas Partnerships About Us News & Media Novavax Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Operational Highlights August 6, 2026 Reported total revenue of $57 million for the second quarter of 2026 and raised full-year 2026 Revenue Framework Improved GAAP Combined R&D and SG&A expense guidance by $10 million at mid-point Sanofi confirmed with Novavax that they are in advanced discussions with regulators regarding their Phase 3 COVID-19-Influenza Combination trial timing and intend to be among the first movers in the combination vaccine segment Completion of manufacturing technology transfer to Sanofi expected in mid-2027 and would trigger a $75 million milestone payment to Novavax Multiple partner-led experiments with Matrix-M are currently underway in a wide array of infectious disease and oncology targets On track to advance C. difficile vaccine program into the clinic as early as 2027 GAITHERSBURG, Md. , Aug. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Novavax, Inc. (Nasdaq: NVAX) today announced its financial results and operational highlights for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026. "We're encouraged by the momentum we're seeing across our business as we continue to advance our strategy," said John C. Jacobs, President and Chief Executive Officer, Novavax. "As we enter the second half of 2026 and prepare for next year, we believe we are well positioned to deliver several important partner milestones while we advance our internal R&D programs and progress our MTA collaborations. This continued progress reinforces our confidence in our strategy and the potential to drive vaccine innovation to create meaningful value for our shareholders." Second Quarter 2026 and Recent Highlights Key Business Highlights Sanofi partnership continues to advance, supporting significant potential near- and long-term value creation. Sanofi confirmed with Novavax they intend to be among the first movers in the combination vaccine segment and that they are in advanced discussions with regulators regarding their Phase 3 COVID-19-Influenza Combination (CIC) trial timing. Initiation of this trial in the U.S. or European Union will trigger a $125 million milestone to Novavax. Manufacturing technology transfer to Sanofi for Nuvaxovid™ is expected to be completed in mid-2027, which would trigger a $75 million milestone payment to Novavax. Sanofi is expanding the commercial reach of Nuvaxovid through broader commercial activities in the U.S. and launches in the United Kingdom, Germany and Canada from 2026 onwards, with Novavax eligible to receive royalties in the high teens to low twenties as a percentage of Sanofi's global net sales. Sanofi received Fast Track designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for its H5 pandemic influenza vaccine candidate (SP0335) utilizing Matrix-M®. A growing body of scientific evidence supports Matrix-M's utility in oncology and infectious disease. Multiple scientific evaluations by partners and potential partners are underway, enabling future licensing opportunities. Advanced Novavax's differentiated C. difficile vaccine candidate into pre-IND interactions with the FDA and initiated GMP manufacturing process, supporting potential clinical entry as early as 2027. Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results Total revenue for the second quarter of 2026 was $57 million, a 76% decrease compared to $239 million in the same period in 2025. body_text: Apartments.com and CoStar Release a Multifamily Vacancy Update for Q2 2026 August 6, 2026 PDF Version ARLINGTON, Va.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Aug. 6, 2026-- Today, Apartments.com and CoStar , the leading global provider of online real estate marketplaces, information and analytics in the property markets, released its latest update on U.S. multifamily vacancy trends, showing improving market conditions as apartment demand continues to absorb the recent wave of new supply. This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260806704186/en/ US apartment vacancy declines from recent high The national apartment vacancy rate declined to 8.2% in the second quarter of 2026, down 26 basis points from the prior quarter and 14 basis points from one year earlier. The improvement reflects stronger renter demand and a moderation in apartment deliveries as the industry's construction pipeline continues to shrink. U.S. apartment absorption totaled approximately 164,000 units during the second quarter, a 13% increase from one year ago. At the same time, apartment deliveries fell to roughly 118,000 units, down 22% year over year. As a result, demand exceeded new supply by more than 45,000 units during the quarter. "Apartment market conditions continued to improve during the second quarter as renter demand remained healthy while new supply pressures eased," said Grant Montgomery, national director of U.S. multifamily analytics at CoStar Group. "Although operating conditions vary across markets, the national supply-demand balance has become increasingly favorable over the past year." The improvement comes as apartment construction activity continues to contract nationally. Annual apartment deliveries have begun to moderate from recent highs and are expected to continue trending lower as fewer projects remain under construction. Regional performance remained uneven during the second quarter. The Northeast and Pacific regions reported the lowest vacancy rates at 5.1% and 5.7%, respectively, while vacancy rates remained highest in the South (at 10.8%) and Mountain region (at 10.2%). Despite those differences, vacancy rates generally stabilized or improved across many markets as new supply pressures eased. Market conditions remain uneven across the country, though several high-supply markets have begun to show improvement as construction activity slows. Austin's vacancy rate declined to 12.3% in the second quarter, nearly 300 basis points below year-ago levels as new deliveries fell sharply. Raleigh also posted a notable improvement, with vacancy declining more than 240 basis points year over year to 9.0% as supply pressures eased. The full analysis can be found here . body_text: Fake medicines are putting UK patients at risk The NHS has issued an urgent warning to people across the UK about the growing threat of fake medicines being sold through unregulated websites, social media platforms, and other unofficial sellers. As more people turn to the internet to purchase healthcare products, weight loss treatments, supplements, and medical devices, criminals are increasingly using fake online pharmacies and copied websites to sell unsafe products. These counterfeit medicines may not contain the correct ingredients, may be contaminated, or could be completely different from what is advertised. Health professionals are urging patients to be cautious and only buy medicines from trusted and registered sources. A simple check before purchasing can help prevent serious health risks and ensure that people receive safe and effective treatment. Why fake medicines are becoming a growing problem Online shopping has made it easier than ever to access healthcare products, but it has also created opportunities for dishonest sellers. Some websites are designed to look like legitimate pharmacies, making it difficult for customers to identify whether they are genuine. Fake online pharmacies may use professional-looking websites, misleading advertisements, and unrealistic offers to attract buyers. Some even copy the branding and appearance of trusted healthcare providers. Weight loss medicines have become a particular concern, with many products being promoted through social media advertisements and unofficial websites. Some sellers claim their products offer quick results without requiring medical checks or a prescription. However, medicines that are supplied without proper medical assessment can be dangerous. Patients may not know what ingredients they are taking, whether the product is suitable for their health condition, or whether it could interact with other medicines. NHS advice: Always use registered healthcare providers NHS Thames Valley is encouraging people to avoid buying medicines and medical devices from websites or businesses that are not regulated. Medicines that require a prescription should only be obtained through a qualified healthcare professional, such as a GP or registered pharmacy. Buying these products from unknown sources can expose patients to serious risks. Olivier Picard, a Thames Valley pharmacist and Chair of the National Pharmacy Association, highlighted the increasing sophistication of fake online pharmacies. Criminal sellers are becoming better at creating websites that appear genuine and trustworthy. He warned that medicines advertised online, especially weight loss treatments, may be counterfeit, contaminated, unsafe, or contain ingredients that are different from those listed in advertisements. The advice from healthcare experts is clear: if an offer appears too good to be true, it may not be safe. How to identify a safe online pharmacy Before purchasing any medicine online, patients should take time to check whether the seller is legitimate. The General Pharmaceutical Council (GPhC) maintains a register of approved pharmacies operating in the UK. Checking this register is one of the most important steps consumers can take before buying medicines online. A trustworthy online pharmacy should: • Be registered with the General Pharmaceutical Council • Clearly display registration details • Require appropriate medical checks for prescription medicines • Provide access to qualified healthcare professionals • Avoid making unrealistic claims about products Customers should be especially careful when websites offer prescription medicines without asking for medical information or provide large discounts that seem unusual. Social media advertisements can be misleading Many fake medicine sellers now use social media platforms to promote their products. Advertisements may feature dramatic claims, customer testimonials, or promises of fast results. While some online health information can be useful, social media advertisements are not always reviewed by healthcare professionals. A product promoted online does not automatically mean it is safe, approved, or effective. Health experts recommend avoiding medicines purchased through social media sellers unless the seller can be verified as a registered healthcare provider. Patients should also avoid sharing personal health information with unknown sellers or websites that do not have proper security and privacy measures. What to do if you have bought a suspicious medicine People who are concerned about a medicine they purchased online should not ignore the issue. Speaking with a community pharmacist is a good first step. Pharmacists are trained healthcare professionals who can provide advice about medicines, identify potential concerns, and recommend what action should be taken. Patients should seek medical advice if they experience unusual symptoms after taking a medicine from an unfamiliar source. They should also keep any packaging, receipts, or information about where the product was purchased, as this may help healthcare professionals investigate the issue. If a medicine looks different from expected, has unusual packaging, contains spelling mistakes, or arrives from an unknown supplier, it may be a warning sign. Protecting your health when buying medicines online The internet can provide convenient access to healthcare products, but convenience should never come at the cost of safety. Before buying any medicine online, patients should ask themselves a few important questions: • Is the website registered and regulated? • Does the seller require proper medical checks? • Is the price unusually low compared with trusted providers? • Are there clear contact details and professional information? • Are claims being made that sound unrealistic? Taking a few minutes to verify a seller could prevent serious health problems and protect people from counterfeit medicines. Healthcare professionals continue to encourage patients to seek advice from GPs, pharmacists, and regulated healthcare providers whenever they have concerns about medicines or treatments. Final thoughts The NHS warning about fake medicines highlights the importance of being careful when purchasing healthcare products online. Counterfeit medicines are not just ineffective, they can also pose serious risks to people’s health. As online scams become more advanced, checking the legitimacy of a pharmacy has become an essential step for every patient. Using registered providers, seeking professional medical advice, and avoiding suspicious online offers can help ensure that people receive safe and effective treatment. Your health should always come before convenience. When it comes to medicines, choosing a trusted source is one of the simplest ways to stay protected. Source NHS Thames Valley warning about fake medicines and advice from healthcare professionals, including representatives from NHS Thames Valley, the National Pharmacy Association, and the General Pharmaceutical Council. Disclaimer This blog is for general information purposes only and does not replace professional medical advice. Always consult a qualified healthcare professional, GP, or pharmacist before starting, stopping, or changing any medication. If you believe you have taken a counterfeit or unsafe medicine, seek advice from a healthcare professional as soon as possible.

title: My First DEF CON: A Different Way of Looking at Security
summary: Joe Knight shares what stood out during his first DEF CON, from hacker culture and physical security to the growing attack surface.
body_text: Joe Knight, Senior Account Director August 18, 2026 “ Security does not stop at traditional IT environments. “ Key Takeaways DEF CON gave me a much better sense of how large and varied the cybersecurity community really is. Security reaches far beyond laptops, servers, and networks. I saw it applied to everything from vehicles and industrial systems to satellites and physical access. Some of the most interesting moments came from watching people find weaknesses simply by approaching a problem differently. I was impressed by how willing people were to share what they knew, even with someone they had just met. I left with more things I want to learn about than when I arrived, which may be my biggest takeaway from the entire experience. Walking into registration was my first real “wow” moment. I knew DEF CON was big, but seeing the sheer number of people there was different from hearing about it. It gave me an immediate sense of just how large the cybersecurity community is and how many different interests and specialties exist within it. I expected to see security professionals and researchers. I did not expect the range of people I encountered: hobbyists, hardware hackers, lock-picking enthusiasts, ham radio operators, automotive security experts, and people working in areas I had never really connected with cybersecurity before. That variety ended up being one of the best parts of the experience. A Very Different Kind of Conference I attend a fair number of conferences for work, and DEF CON did not feel like any of them. Even the vendor area was unlike what I was used to seeing at other conferences. It did not feel like a traditional trade show. There were tools, hardware, projects, experiments, and plenty of things I had never seen before. More than anything, it felt like a showcase of the creativity and hacker culture that make DEF CON so different from a traditional industry conference. I found several cybersecurity tools and projects that I want to spend more time exploring on my own. For me, that was part of the fun of DEF CON. You could come across something you knew almost nothing about, start asking questions, and usually find someone who was happy to walk you through it. That happened throughout the conference. People were open about sharing what they knew, including with people they had just met. They talked through techniques, lessons learned, and things they had discovered along the way. For a first-time attendee, that made DEF CON feel much more approachable than I expected. Some of my best conversations also happened after the sessions ended. The evening events and parties gave me a chance to meet people I probably never would have crossed paths with otherwise. I talked with people from different industries, roles, and technical specialties, and the conversations felt much more informal than the networking you usually get at a business conference. People talked about what they were building, what they were learning, how they got into security, and what they had seen that day. Those conversations were a big part of the experience for me. Security Goes Far Beyond IT Day two probably changed my perspective more than anything else at the conference. I am used to hearing cybersecurity discussed in terms of endpoints, networks, cloud environments, applications, email, and data. At DEF CON, I was watching people work with cars, semi-trucks, boats, aviation technology, satellites, weather systems, industrial systems, and wireless communications. Seeing all of that in one place made the size of the attack surface much more tangible. One minute you could be looking at vehicle security, and not long after that you could be learning about satellites or aviation systems. Seeing that range firsthand made me realize how many technologies around us now have a cybersecurity component. That was one of the biggest shifts for me. Security does not stop at traditional IT environments. It is built into far more of the physical world than I had really appreciated before attending DEF CON. The Physical Security Villages Stood Out I also spent time around the physical security villages, which was one of the more surprising parts of the conference. Learning some of the lock bypass and entry techniques firsthand gave me a completely different perspective on physical security. That was one of those moments when a familiar cybersecurity idea became much more real to me. A control can work exactly as designed and still have weaknesses if you only think about how it is supposed to be used. Good security requires thinking about how someone might get around it. What surprised me was how often creativity mattered just as much as technical knowledge. Sometimes the weakness was highly technical. Other times, someone simply looked at the problem differently. Creativity Matters More Than I Expected One thing I did not fully appreciate before DEF CON was how much creativity goes into finding security weaknesses. The technical expertise was obviously impressive, but just as interesting was seeing the way people approached problems. They would look at something that appeared to work exactly as intended and ask a completely different question about it. What else could this do? What happens if I use it differently? What happens if someone uses it in a way the designer never expected? That way of thinking stuck with me. Sometimes finding a vulnerability starts with deep technical expertise. Other times it starts because someone was curious enough to question something everyone else had accepted. That is something I can take back to my own role as well. Even if you are not the person testing the system, there is a lot of value in understanding how attackers think. There Is a Community For Almost Everything I also had no idea how many specialized communities existed inside DEF CON. Ham radio, wireless communications, hardware hacking, lock picking, gaming security, automotive systems—the list seemed endless. You could walk from one area to another and suddenly find yourself learning about a completely different corner of cybersecurity. That was part of what made DEF CON so valuable for me. It exposed me to subjects I would not normally encounter in my day-to-day work. It also reinforced something I kept noticing throughout the conference: security is everywhere. Almost any device, system, or process has a security angle worth examining. What I Took Away From My First DEF CON I left DEF CON with a longer list of things I want to learn about than when I arrived. I walked into DEF CON impressed by the size of the cybersecurity community. I left even more impressed by how much there still is to learn from it. One lesson I kept coming back to was just how broad an attack surface can be. Across traditional IT, operational technology, physical security, and connected systems, risk can exist in places organizations may not immediately think to look. Understanding where that exposure exists is an important first step toward reducing it. ns about confidentiality or privilege. Employees should consult legal counsel before using an AI tool for legal documents or case-related information. Security Is Everywhere. Are You Seeing the Big Picture?
