Conta PJ digital na prática para organizar vendas, despesas e decisões do negócio
summary: Entenda como funciona uma conta PJ digital na prática, reunindo recebimentos, pagamentos, cartões, reservas e permissões no mesmo ambiente.
body_text: A venda cai hoje, o fornecedor vence amanhã e a equipe precisa comprar insumo antes do almoço. Se cada tarefa pede um aplicativo, uma senha e uma conferência separada, o dono vira ponte entre tudo. É aí que a conta empresarial começa a organizar o trabalho, não só o dinheiro. Uma conta PJ digital é uma conta empresarial movimentada pelo celular, criada para separar e organizar o dinheiro do CNPJ . Ela simplifica a rotina quando reúne recebimentos, pagamentos, cartões, reservas e permissões no mesmo ambiente. Com a Stone, o banco para quem empreende, você conecta esses recursos às vendas do negócio, da maquininha ao link de pagamento. Assim, você acompanha o que entrou, decide o que pode sair e separa o dinheiro que já tem destino sem precisar caçar números em vários lugares. Uma boa conta reduz trocas de aplicativo ao longo do dia Quem tem a barriga no balcão não precisa de uma função bonita escondida no menu. Precisa receber, pagar, conferir e decidir sem interromper a operação a cada movimentação. O melhor recurso é o que elimina uma etapa manual da rotina. Pode ser a transferência que você deixa de fazer entre duas instituições, o comprovante que não precisa buscar no WhatsApp ou a despesa da equipe que não passa mais pelo cartão pessoal. Comece pelo caminho que o dinheiro percorre. De manhã, você precisa saber qual valor está disponível. Durante o expediente, precisa acompanhar as vendas e fazer pagamentos. Antes de fechar, precisa entender o que ainda vai entrar e quanto já está comprometido com estoque, contas e outras obrigações. Na Conta PJ Stone , você reúne a movimentação financeira e os recebimentos das vendas no mesmo app. Não cobramos mensalidade na conta, e os valores das vendas feitas pela maquininha seguem direto para ela conforme o prazo de recebimento contratado. Quando o plano prevê recebimento no dia seguinte, por exemplo, o dinheiro das vendas de cartão cai diretamente na conta. Isso evita uma transferência posterior e deixa mais claro quanto da venda já está disponível para movimentar. Uma leitura útil separa três valores: O saldo disponível responde ao que pode ser usado agora; O saldo a receber mostra vendas que ainda vão cair; Já o dinheiro comprometido inclui valores que estão na conta, mas pertencem a uma despesa futura. Essa diferença parece pequena até chegar o dia do aluguel, do imposto ou da reposição de estoque. Se todo saldo positivo for tratado como dinheiro livre, uma compra feita hoje pode apertar o caixa da semana seguinte. A conta digital ajuda justamente porque coloca essas informações mais perto da decisão. Você não precisa esperar o fechamento mensal para descobrir que vendeu bem, mas gastou antes da hora. Receber e pagar no mesmo ambiente melhora a leitura do caixa Cada canal de venda resolve uma situação diferente. A maquininha atende o balcão. O Pix funciona bem para pagamentos rápidos. O link de pagamento leva a venda para o WhatsApp , redes sociais ou atendimento remoto. O Banco Central explica que o Pix transfere recursos em poucos segundos, a qualquer hora ou dia . Essa disponibilidade ajuda a confirmar pagamentos fora do horário bancário e reduz a espera entre a venda e a entrada do dinheiro. O ganho operacional aparece quando esses recebimentos chegam à conta usada para pagar as despesas do negócio. Você evita mandar dinheiro de um lado para o outro antes de quitar um fornecedor, fazer um Pix ou pagar uma conta. Receber e pagar no mesmo ambiente deixa o caminho do dinheiro mais fácil de acompanhar. A venda entra vinculada ao CNPJ, a despesa sai da conta empresarial e o extrato passa a contar uma história mais fiel da operação. Pense em uma loja que vende no balcão, recebe pedidos pelo WhatsApp e mantém um pequeno catálogo online . Se cada canal cair em uma conta diferente, o fechamento depende de várias consultas. Quando os recebimentos seguem para o mesmo lugar, fica mais fácil comparar o movimento dos canais e planejar os pagamentos. Isso também melhora a conversa com a contabilidade. Um extrato empresarial separado reduz a mistura com supermercado, escola, lazer e outras despesas pessoais. O contador recebe uma movimentação mais limpa, e você ganha uma base melhor para entender o resultado do mês. A organização depende do uso, claro. Uma conta PJ não resolve a gestão se as despesas pessoais continuarem saindo do caixa da empresa. O primeiro passo é direcionar as receitas do negócio para a conta empresarial e definir uma retirada para o dono, em vez de pagar gastos pessoais conforme eles aparecem. Na hora de olhar o extrato, evite considerar toda entrada como lucro. Parte do valor pode corresponder ao custo da mercadoria, às taxas da venda, à folha, aos impostos e às contas que ainda vão vencer. A conta mostra o movimento. A decisão vem da classificação que você faz desse dinheiro. A equipe ganha autonomia quando os limites ficam visíveis Quando toda compra depende do dono, uma operação simples trava. O gerente precisa repor um item, a pessoa do marketing precisa pagar uma ferramenta e o responsável pela manutenção aguarda uma autorização. Enquanto isso, o empreendedor vira o caixa de cada área. Dar autonomia não significa entregar a mesma liberdade para todo mundo. Autonomia boa vem com permissão definida, limite acompanhado e responsabilidade clara. Em uma conta empresarial, acessos com diferentes níveis de permissão ajudam a distribuir tarefas financeiras sem compartilhar a senha principal nem liberar toda a movimentação da empresa. Antes de delegar, defina quem pode consultar, quem pode preparar uma transação e quem pode aprovar. Também deixe claro quais compras precisam de validação prévia e como os comprovantes devem ser registrados. O cartão empresarial entra nessa organização porque mantém a despesa dentro da rotina do CNPJ. Em vez de usar o cartão pessoal e pedir reembolso depois, a compra fica associada ao negócio desde o começo. Por isso, a Stone também disponibiliza um Cartão PJ sem anuidade , sendo que a função crédito e o limite dependem de análise de perfil. Essa condição precisa entrar na conta antes de qualquer planejamento de compra ou parcelamento. O cartão virtual pode ser usado em compras online e assinaturas da operação, enquanto o cartão físico acompanha despesas presenciais. O cuidado está em não tratar o limite como extensão do faturamento. Compras parceladas ocupam espaço nas próximas faturas, mesmo quando a venda que vai pagá-las ainda não aconteceu. Uma regra simples ajuda: a despesa delegada precisa ter finalidade definida, responsável identificado e valor compatível com o caixa previsto. Assim, a equipe anda sem transformar o dono em aprovador de cada café ou deixar a operação correr sem controle. O saldo de hoje precisa respeitar as contas de amanhã Uma sexta-feira de vendas fortes pode dar a impressão de caixa folgado. Só que parte daquele dinheiro pode estar comprometida com reposição, manutenção, impostos ou pagamentos da equipe. Se tudo ficar misturado, o saldo cheio convida a decisões que não cabem no mês. Separar o dinheiro antes do vencimento protege a decisão de compra do impulso do saldo cheio. Em vez de esperar sobrar, você define o destino assim que a receita entra. Uma forma prática de organizar a reserva é separar os valores por objetivos financeiros. Dá para destinar dinheiro a despesas previstas, formar uma reserva para imprevistos ou guardar para um investimento na operação. Também vale definir um percentual das vendas diárias como referência para a reserva. Esse hábito acompanha o ritmo do negócio e reduz a dependência de separar todo o valor apenas no fim do mês. Se a reserva ficar em um investimento de renda fixa, confira o emissor, a rentabilidade, a liquidez e a cobertura do FGC antes de aplicar. O CDI é uma taxa de referência usada nesse tipo de investimento, mas as condições variam conforme o produto escolhido. A garantia do FGC segue limites e critérios próprios, inclusive o teto de até R$ 250 mil por CPF ou CNPJ, por instituição ou conglomerado financeiro. Por isso, a proteção precisa ser analisada considerando todos os produtos elegíveis mantidos no mesmo conglomerado. O percentual destinado à reserva deve respeitar a margem e o calendário do negócio. Uma loja com reposição diária precisa de mais dinheiro livre do que uma empresa que compra insumos uma vez por mês. Comece com um valor que caiba no giro e ajuste conforme o histórico das entradas e saídas. Essa separação também melhora a leitura do saldo. O dinheiro da conta atende à operação corrente, e o valor guardado tem um objetivo definido. Quando surge uma oportunidade de comprar estoque com desconto ou trocar um equipamento, você consegue avaliar o investimento sem confundir recursos de finalidades diferentes. O teste final acontece antes de fechar o caixa Uma boa conta PJ digital precisa responder, em poucos minutos, quanto entrou, o que ainda vai cair, quanto pode ser usado e quais valores já têm destino. Se essas respostas continuam espalhadas por planilhas, extratos e conversas, ainda existe trabalho manual demais no caminho. Antes de encerrar o dia, confira os recebimentos, os pagamentos realizados, as movimentações da equipe e o valor separado para despesas futuras. Não precisa transformar isso em um projeto. A rotina curta e repetida costuma mostrar desvios antes que eles cresçam. E aí, sua conta está simplificando a operação ou só levou a papelada para a tela? A resposta aparece quando você consegue tomar uma decisão sem abrir três aplicativos, pedir um comprovante no grupo ou fazer uma transferência só para começar outra tarefa. Na Conta PJ Stone, você reúne maquininha, Pix, link de pagamento, Cartão PJ e reservas no mesmo app, sem mensalidade. O ganho aparece quando cada recurso tira uma etapa do seu caminho e devolve uma decisão mais clara para o negócio. Este conteúdo é uma forma de apoiar empreendedores na sua jornada. No entanto, cada estabelecimento é único, e nem todas as dicas aqui podem se aplicar ao seu negócio.

title: flexABILITY and Making Room for What Matters
summary: Learn how Louis Sorrell personalized the Langford floorplan with flexABILITY to create a home that reflects his family's lifestyle.
body_text: Posted by Reyna Estrada in Minneapolis , Happy Homeowners ) The Foundation Why Louis Chose the Langford—and Why the Standard Plan Was Already So Strong Although the video opens with Louis’s cigar lounge — one of the most personal spaces in the home — the story actually begins with the Langford floorplan itself. Before any custom touches, Louis chose a standard plan strong enough to support both everyday living and the unique spaces that came later. Every home tells a story. For Louis Sorrell and his family, that story began with a simple goal: build a home that reflects the way they actually live. Not an idealized version of life, but the real, everyday rhythms that make a home feel personal. As his children reached college age and the family transitioned into the empty nester phase, Louis began searching for what he calls a “right sized” home—one designed for this next chapter, not simply a smaller version of what they had before. After 28 years selling new construction, he knew exactly how often homeowners end up wishing they had made different choices. This time, he wanted clarity from the start. That clarity came when he found M/I Homes’ Langford floorplan . With its main level lifestyle, open gathering spaces, and smart flow, the standard plan already aligned with the way the Sorrells lived. It didn’t need reinvention—it needed permission to be personalized. That’s where flexABILITY made the difference. Instead of forcing his lifestyle into a rigid layout or redesigning a home from scratch, Louis could take a strong, well designed foundation and refine it with intention. The Langford gave him the structure he trusted; flexABILITY gave him the freedom to shape it around the routines, passions, and gatherings that define everyday life. With the foundation in place, Louis turned his attention to the spaces where life actually happens—and that’s where the home truly came to life. Everyday Living How flexABILITY Personalized the Spaces the Family Uses Most With the Langford as a strong foundation, flexABILITY gave Louis the freedom to shape everyday spaces around the way his family truly lives. Rather than making sweeping changes, he focused on refining the areas they use most, creating a home that feels intentional, comfortable, and personal. The Kitchen: A Gathering Place, Not Just a Workspace The open concept kitchen naturally connected cooking, dining, and gathering, and Louis leaned into that strength. Instead of keeping a formal dining room they rarely used, the Sorrells invested in the space where life actually happens. By extending the center island to seat seven and adding a walk up wet bar, they transformed the kitchen into the true heart of the home—a place where meals, conversations, games, and everyday moments unfold without effort. It didn’t become the heart of the home because it was bigger. It became the heart because it was designed around how they gather. A Mud Room Designed Around Family—Including the Four-Legged Kind The mud room offered a practical transition from the garage, but Louis saw an opportunity to make it work harder. With a barn door and a thoughtful reconfiguration, an ordinary storage area became a dedicated retreat for their Maltipoo. It’s a small change, but a perfect example of flexABILITY: taking everyday spaces and shaping them around the people—and pets—who use them. A Great Room That Reflects Their Style Louis wanted the great room to match his family’s contemporary aesthetic. As a self described “big TV guy,” he replaced the traditional gas fireplace with a sleek linear electric model that allowed a large television to be mounted cleanly above it. Wrapped in crisp white shiplap, the feature adds modern character while keeping the focus exactly where the family enjoys spending time together. Extending Everyday Living Outdoors The Sorrells wanted indoor and outdoor living to feel equally intentional. With the home’s southern exposure, they selected the largest available deck, added wide steps to a stamped patio, and created a welcoming fire pit area for casual gatherings. Like the rest of the home, these outdoor spaces weren’t designed for special occasions—they were built to be part of everyday life. Beyond Everyday Living How flexABILITY Made Room for Passions, Hospitality, and Life's Next Chapter A well-designed floorplan should support everyday routines. The Langford already provided the strong foundation the Sorrell family needed for this next stage of life. flexABILITY allowed them to build on that foundation, creating spaces that reflected their hobbies, hospitality, and the way they wanted to enjoy their home for years to come. Some spaces are about function. Others are about pure enjoyment. Louis’s basement cigar lounge is both. After unexpectedly developing a passion for cigars, Louis wanted a dedicated, private space where he could unwind without affecting the rest of the household. One of the Langford's unfinished basement spaces became an opportunity rather than simply extra square footage, thanks to a collaborative brainstorming session with one of the team's draftsmen. Working alongside M/I's drafting team, Louis collaborated on a custom exhaust system that completely seals the room, pulling smoke away before it reaches the rest of the home. The result is a flawless seal: the exhaust completely pulls the smoke away, leaving the main living areas entirely free of odor. The cigar lounge illustrates what makes the combination of the Langford floorplan and flexABILITY so compelling. A thoughtfully designed home provides an exceptional starting point. The ability to personalize it means those spaces can evolve into something uniquely your own. In the depths of a hard Minnesota winter, having the freedom to step downstairs, pour a glass of scotch, and enjoy a premium cigar in total comfort is, as Louis says, "everything in the moment." ﻿ Tags home upgrades homeowner Author Reyna Estrada Author Reyna Estrada has been with M/I Homes since 2008. title: Trimble Introduces Trimble Arc Agent to Safely Automate Manual Workflows for Global Supply Chains
summary: The single, high-performance AI agent moves beyond the limitations of multi-agent setups The solution offers an expanding, customizable skills catalog designed with governance controls and risk...
body_text: The single, high-performance AI agent moves beyond the limitations of multi-agent setups The solution offers an expanding, customizable skills catalog designed with governance controls and risk review workflows WESTMINSTER, Colo. , Aug. 11, 2026 / PRNewswire / -- Trimble announced today Trimble Arc Agent, a purpose-built artificial intelligence (AI) agent designed to automate office work and eliminate manual processes for transportation and logistics organizations. By reducing reliance on multiple agents, Trimble Arc Agent frees teams to focus on high-level strategy where human decision-making matters most. Offered as a subscription-based software-as-a-service (SaaS) solution, Trimble Arc Agent connects directly to existing transportation management systems (TMS) and third-party applications like Gmail and Outlook. By securely extracting and validating data from unstructured channels — such as emails, PDFs and spreadsheets — Trimble Arc Agent allows teams to turn real-world inputs into actionable, system-of-record data. For many logistics teams, unstructured data and multi-agent setups inhibit productivity due to busy work, where teams spend more time managing software than driving strategy. According to a recent survey conducted by Trimble and FreightWaves, 70% of transportation and logistics organizations struggle with manual, repetitive tasks as their leading pain point, stifling staff productivity. Trimble Arc Agent bridges the gap between the physical supply chain and digital back-office systems by automating the flow of information. Built with core agentic safety features to minimize the risk of AI hallucinations, Trimble Arc Agent empowers organizations to drive faster throughput and reduce operational costs without compromising service levels or margins. "The market is flooded with disconnected AI tools that require constant babysitting and manual management. We built Trimble Arc Agent to break that cycle by introducing a single, high-performance agent powered by a skills catalog," said Jonah McIntire, chief product and technology officer, transportation and logistics at Trimble. "Arc Agent delivers the predictable, explainable automation the industry has been waiting for and allows for an organization's hard-earned operational knowledge to be retained and executed consistently." Safety and reliability by design Trimble Arc Agent is designed with safety in mind, with enterprise-grade AI guardrails and human-in-the-loop controls, designed to ensure that AI-driven decisions are explainable, auditable and supportable. This approach addresses industry concerns regarding AI reliability so that automation does not come at the cost of service commitments or compliance. The power of the Trimble Arc Agent skills catalog Arc Agent brings high-level automation to an industry at scale — deployed across the Trimble transportation and logistics network of more than one million trucks and over 1,500 shippers and retailers — in addition to a wide range of back-office tools and applications. Central to Arc Agent is the creation, discovery and leveraging of skills. By combining a catalog of ready-to-use skills with custom skill-building capabilities, Arc Agent can help address an organization's biggest challenges through simple, natural language. Beyond these ready-to-use offerings, Trimble Arc empowers teams with intuitive, custom skill-building capabilities. Users can easily adapt existing skills to fit their unique operational needs or build entirely new ones via a conversational interface — without requiring any engineering resources. Example skills include: Data Entry (Order Entry & Contract Intake): This skill provides an alternative to manual order entry and contract intake by automatically extracting field data and inputting it directly into systems of record. (Available in North America) Market Insights: This skill delivers full truckload (FTL) rate intelligence and market benchmarks before every negotiation. title: Martes de Glamour: Howdy's Community Went Ringside in Guadalajara
summary: A recap of Martes de Glamour, Howdy's live lucha libre night in Guadalajara: the numbers, the feedback, and why the community called it a favorite.
body_text: On August 4th, we hosted Lucha Libre Night in Guadalajara, an exclusive Howdy experience built for developers and tech professionals in the city. No conference hall, no mic and slides. We boarded a party bus, toasted with a welcome cocktail, and closed the night in premium seats at Arena Coliseo, watching live lucha libre, one of Mexico's most iconic traditions. A Party Bus, a Cocktail, and the Arena Coliseo Ring The night opened with something you rarely see at a tech event: a party bus winding through Guadalajara while the group got to know each other before even arriving. No forced icebreakers, no name tags. By the time we stepped off the bus, conversations were already underway. Inside the arena, the energy shifted completely. Luchador masks on, food and drinks moving around, and the ring giving everyone a reason to look up from their phone. Anyone who has watched live lucha libre for the first time knows the feeling: the noise, the theatrics, people jumping out of their seats. That energy spread fast among developers who, an hour earlier, had never met. View this post on Instagram What the Community Valued Most We asked attendees what stuck with them, and the answers repeated: the lucha libre concept itself, described as original and memorable, the food and atmosphere, and above all, the chance to genuinely connect with developers from different backgrounds. One guest mentioned that the Howdy team went out of its way to help when a friend arrived late, a small moment that says more about the night than any headline act could. One piece of feedback stood out for its simplicity: "The lucha libre idea was very original and made the experience much more fun and memorable." Another guest put it this way: "It felt like a great opportunity to connect with Howdy's team and developers in general." And someone closed with an "excellent organization, thank you so much for the invitation" that, coming from someone who had never heard of Howdy before that night, means more than any metric on a slide. The Numbers Behind the Night Speaking of metrics: the night delivered results that confirm what we suspected. Of the 108 leads registered, 56 qualified as MQLs, and among the 36 attendees, 22 were MQLs, a nearly 52% lead-to-MQL conversion rate. Almost half of the people who showed up at Arena Coliseo had never heard of Howdy before: 46.3% were new audience, while the remaining 53.7% already knew the brand. The satisfaction score closed at 98.6% out of 5, and 100% of respondents said this kind of event helps outsiders get to know Howdy better. Why We Keep Building Nights Like This At Howdy, we believe the best connections happen outside office hours and far from a LinkedIn form. A lucha libre night doesn't replace a technical talk or a meetup, but it does something those formats don't always manage: it lowers the guard, gives people a genuinely unusual shared experience, and sends everyone home with real contacts instead of just a fresh set of digital cards. Guadalajara now has its own Martes de Glamour. The next stop isn't confirmed yet, but if this night taught us anything, it's that LATAM's tech community responds better to a luchador mask than to a corporate flyer.

title: 2026 “Leno’s Law” Clears Committee Where Last Year’s Effort Died
summary: Owners of classic cars in California are inching closer to less stringent emissions requirements. Senate Bill 1392, which would provide a full exemption from smog check requirements for pre-1981 vehicles, has passed from the California Senate to the Assembly, where it has cleared the Appropriations Committee, the same place that a similar version of the […]
body_text: Owners of classic cars in California are inching closer to less stringent emissions requirements. Senate Bill 1392 , which would provide a full exemption from smog check requirements for pre-1981 vehicles, has passed from the California Senate to the Assembly, where it has cleared the Appropriations Committee, the same place that a similar version of the bill (SB 712) died a quiet, procedural death in 2025. Though SB 1392 isn’t on Gavin Newsom’s desk, this milestone is worth celebrating. SB1392 represents the fourth time in 10 years that California legislators have introduced a bill that would relax their state’s strict smog-check requirements for older vehicles. This is the furthest that such a bill has ever gotten: SB 1239 was held on the Senate floor in 2016, AB 467 was held in the Assembly Transportation Committee in 2022, and SB 712 was held on the suspense file in the Assembly Appropriations Committee last year. Unsplash | Tom Shamberger Both last year’s bill and this year’s have been known as “Leno’s Law,” thanks to enthusiastic backing from our favorite car-obsessed comedian, Jay Leno. We reported in the spring that this year’s bill refines last year’s by focusing on the vehicle rather than the owner, and on whether the vehicle in question is that person’s daily driver. In particular, SB 1392 makes life easier for owners of cars built between 1976 and 1986: First, by removing the existing (and partial) smog-check inspection process for collector vehicles built before 1981 (but after 1975, the most recent model year that’s currently exempt) and, second, by expanding the cutoff by one additional model year beginning on January 1, 2028, until January 1, 2032, when the exemption would apply to “qualifying collector motor vehicles” manufacturer before model-year 1986. What’s a qualifying collector motor vehicle, under SB 1392? A vehicle that is “at least 35 MYs old and either insured as a collector motor vehicle with proof of insurance submitted to the Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) at the time of registration, or determined, through a process developed by DMV, to be driven fewer than 1,000 miles per calendar year.” California residents will be happy to remind you that their state used to have a 30-year rolling exemption, until then-governor Arnold Schwarzenegger repealed it in 2004 and applied the smog-check exemption “strictly to vehicles manufactured prior to model year 1976.” If passed into law, “Leno’s Law 2.0” would undoubtedly make life easier for the owners of California’s collector cars, especially the Malaise-Era ones, and that is an outcome well worth celebrating. body_text: View all news Natera Submits Signatera™ to Japan’s PMDA for Approval as a Companion Diagnostic in Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer 08/05/2026 Download (opens in new window) PDF 120 KB Follows Signatera’s recent U.S. FDA approval in MIBC and Japanese PMDA approval in CRC AUSTIN, Texas--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Natera, Inc. (NASDAQ: NTRA), a global leader in cell-free DNA and precision medicine, today announced that it has submitted an application to Japan’s Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency (PMDA) for approval of the Signatera test in muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) as a companion diagnostic (CDx). The submission advances Natera’s growing presence in Japan, where Signatera received PMDA approval in colorectal cancer in June, becoming the country’s first PMDA-approved molecular residual disease (MRD) test. The MIBC application is supported by data from IMvigor011, a randomized, double-blind Phase 3 clinical trial. It also builds on recent milestones for Signatera in MIBC: the U.S. FDA’s approval of Signatera™ CDx as a companion diagnostic for adjuvant atezolizumab (Tecentriq®); and a Category 1 recommendation for Signatera MRD-guided adjuvant atezolizumab in the National Comprehensive Cancer Network® (NCCN®) Clinical Practice Guidelines for Bladder Cancer. Bladder cancer affects more than 34,000 people in Japan each year.1 Globally, approximately 20–25% of newly diagnosed bladder cancers are muscle-invasive.2 MIBC is a more aggressive form of the disease, associated with higher recurrence risk and treatment complexity. “Signatera is a proven tool in bladder cancer management, and this submission reflects our commitment to bringing precision diagnostics to patients in Japan,” said Alexey Aleshin, M.D., corporate chief medical officer and general manager of oncology at Natera. “We look forward to engaging with the PMDA and to improving outcomes for patients around the world.” Notes Tecentriq® (atezolizumab) is a registered trademark of Genentech, a member of the Roche Group. References World Cancer Research Fund International. Bladder cancer statistics. Accessed June 26, 2026. https://www.wcrf.org/preventing-cancer/cancer-statistics/bladder-cancer-statistics/ Gakis G. Management of Muscle-invasive Bladder Cancer in the 2020s: Challenges and Perspectives. Eur. Urol. Focus. 2020;6(4):632-638. About Natera Natera is a global leader in cell-free DNA and precision medicine, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. We aim to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard-of-care to protect health and inform earlier, more targeted interventions that help lead to longer, healthier lives. Natera’s tests are supported by more than 400 peer-reviewed publications that demonstrate excellent performance. Natera operates ISO 13485-certified and CAP-accredited laboratories certified under the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) in Austin, Texas, and San Carlos, California, and through Foresight Diagnostics, its subsidiary, operates an ISO 27001-certified and CAP-accredited laboratory certified under CLIA in Boulder, Colorado. For more information, visit www.natera.com . (NASDAQ: LFCR) (“Lifecore”), a fully integrated injectables contract development and manufacturing organization (“CDMO”), today announced results for the second quarter and six months ended June 30, 2026. CEO Commentary “The second quarter was highly productive. The effectiveness of our new business development strategy has helped us grow the value of our pipeline with consistent wins that point to our manufacturing expertise as well as our exceptional track record in quality and compliance. In addition, Lifecore continues to transition our development pipeline toward commercialization and invest in the talent, processes, and improvements that we believe will support our growing pipeline in the mid-term and allow us to achieve sustainable, long-term profitability in the future. In the past 12 months, we have added 13 new programs to our pipeline, eight of which are late stage. We expect these programs and their financial contributions to play a significant role in Lifecore’s success in achieving our long-term growth objectives of a 12% revenue CAGR and Adjusted EBITDA* margin targets exceeding 25% by the end of 2029,” stated Paul Josephs, president and chief executive officer of Lifecore. Financial Snapshot and Recent Developments Revenues for the second quarter of 2026 were $34.2 million, a decrease of $2.3 million, or 6.2% compared to $36.4 million for the comparable prior year quarter ended May 25, 2025. Revenues for the six months ended June 30, 2026, were $57.4 million, a decrease of $14.2 million, or 19.9% compared to $71.6 million for the six-month comparable prior year period ended May 25, 2025. Gross profit for the quarter was $12.1 million, a decrease of $1.9 million compared to $14.0 million for the comparable prior year quarter ended May 25, 2025. title: 5 best practices to make collaboration finally click
summary: Having the right tools is the easy part. Getting them to work together, and getting people to actually use them, is where most strategies stall.
body_text: Ask most IT leaders whether their organization has capable collaboration technology, and the answer is yes. They've got phones, they've got chat, they've got Zoom Meetings, they've got AI capabilities, document tools, and workflow automation. What's harder to find is an environment where all of it works together in a way that's intuitive for employees and manageable for IT. Research shows employees use fewer than a third of available collaboration features during meetings, and only half of the features available after them.* Most organizations don't have a capability gap on paper. In practice, the gap is strategic. Organizations that build a deliberate collaboration strategy — one that defines how tools connect, how AI gets governed, and how employees actually adopt new ways of working — tend to create environments that get stronger over time. The ones that don't keep adding complexity and wondering why nothing feels simpler. Here are five principles that separate the two. 1. Stop organizing your stack by tool. Organize it by how work actually moves. Vendors have spent the last few years racing to connect their platforms into something more than a collection of features. The result is that the collaboration landscape has reorganized itself around workflows, not categories. The strategic question for IT isn't which tools you have anymore. It's whether they're connected in a way that reflects how work actually flows through your organization. Before evaluating platforms or adding capabilities, map the workflows your employees depend on. Where does work start? Where does it stall? Where does context get lost between tools? Those answers should drive your platform decisions, not the other way around. 2. Govern AI before your employees do it for you The AI adoption question has already been answered. Employees are using AI in their collaboration tools whether IT planned for it or not. The question is whether IT has a governance framework in place before that usage gets ahead of policy. That means deciding which AI capabilities are available to which employees, how AI-generated content is handled under your data policies, and how you maintain visibility across tools. A platform that centralizes AI governance gives IT the controls to answer those questions. A patchwork of plugins and browser extensions tends to answer them for you, usually at the worst possible time. 3. Make integration a baseline requirement, not a bonus No business is starting from zero. Your employees already use productivity suites, CRM platforms, and communication tools they depend on daily. A modern collaboration strategy connects those investments rather than replacing them. Treat integration as a baseline requirement when evaluating any collaboration platform. The right question isn't whether a platform can integrate with your existing stack. It's how deeply, how reliably, and how much administrative overhead that integration creates over time. A platform that plays well with everything else you run compounds in value. One that requires constant maintenance to stay connected is just another thing to manage. 4. Adoption is a design problem, not a launch problem Between a third and a half of available collaboration functionality, much of it AI-native, goes untapped.* Adoption was never truly designed, and that's one of the main problems. Effective adoption strategies are persona-specific. Executives, managers, and individual contributors use collaboration tools differently and value different capabilities. A rollout that treats all employees the same tends to produce the same result: a few power users and a lot of idle features collecting dust in a settings menu nobody opens. Build adoption into the platform decision. Ask vendors how they support change management, what in-product guidance looks like, and how they measure feature utilization over time, not just license counts. 5. There's likely more value in your collaboration environment than you're capturing Most IT teams evaluate collaboration platforms through meeting counts and uptime metrics: a narrow lens that misses most of where value actually lives. A more complete view includes time saved across the meeting lifecycle, reductions in repeated meetings, speed of decision-making, and how employees actually experience the tools day to day. Many CIOs acknowledge this gap. They know there's more value to measure, but they don't have the instrumentation to capture it.* Platforms that provide visibility into how collaboration is actually being used, not just whether it's being used, give IT the data to demonstrate value, defend investments, and know where to improve before employees start working around the gaps. Ready to see what a stronger collaboration strategy can look like in practice? Strengthen your strategy *Deloitte, commissioned by Zoom, "The Productivity Payoff of Next Generation Collaboration," 2025.

title: Humacyte Announces Lancet Digital Health Publication of V007 Phase 3 Hemodialysis Access Trial Results
summary: – Phase 3 results highlight benefits of ATEV for patients at higher risk of fistula failure, including all women and men with obesity and diabetes – – Publication provides peer-reviewed validation for V007 Phase 3 data, and complements recent release of Phase 3 V012 data showing ATEV outperformed
body_text: PDF Version – Phase 3 results highlight benefits of ATEV for patients at higher risk of fistula failure, including all women and men with obesity and diabetes – – Publication provides peer-reviewed validation for V007 Phase 3 data, and complements recent release of Phase 3 V012 data showing ATEV outperformed standard of care for women on dialysis – DURHAM, N.C., Aug. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Humacyte, Inc. (Nasdaq: HUMA), a commercial-stage biotechnology platform company developing universally implantable, bioengineered human tissues at commercial scale, today announced the publication of one-year results from the V007 Phase 3 clinical trial of the acellular tissue engineered vessel (ATEV) in arteriovenous (AV) access for hemodialysis patients in The Lancet Digital Health, a leading peer-reviewed journal in the Lancet family. The publication, titled "A Multi-center Randomized Trial of a Bioengineered Acellular Tissue Engineered Vessel versus Autogenous Fistula for Hemodialysis Access," demonstrates the positive findings from Humacyte's V007 trial, previously presented at major medical conferences, showing the superiority of the ATEV over autogenous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) for hemodialysis vascular access after one year of follow up, particularly for all female patients and male patients with obesity and diabetes, groups that often face higher rates of AVF failure. "Reliable hemodialysis access is critical for patients with end-stage kidney disease, yet remains a challenge for many, especially those with higher risk profiles," said Mohamad A. Hussain, M.D., Ph.D., lead author of the publication and Vascular and Endovascular Surgeon at Heart and Vascular Institute, Mass General Brigham and Associate Professor of Surgery at Harvard Medical School. "This publication in The Lancet Digital Health provides additional validation of these results and highlights the potential of ATEV as an alternative for patients who may be less likely to benefit from AV fistulas.” “Publication in The Lancet Digital Health is a significant milestone for Humacyte and an important validation of our Phase 3 dialysis data. These results demonstrate that the ATEV can offer a better option for the patients who need it most, particularly all women and men with obesity and diabetes, who too often face poor outcomes with traditional fistulas,” said Laura Niklason, M.D., Ph.D., Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Humacyte. “With the V007 and V012 results we believe we have built a compelling case to bring this technology to the patients who stand to benefit most.” Positive two-year results from the V007 Phase 3 trial, announced in November 2025 at the American Society of Nephrology’s Kidney Week 2025 , further demonstrated the durability of ATEV's benefits over time. Additionally, Humacyte reported top-line interim results from its V012 Phase 3 study June 11, 2026 at the Society of Vascular Surgery’s (SVS) Vascular Annual Meeting (VAM) in Boston. V012 is specifically focused on female patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) needing hemodialysis — a population in which the V007 one-year data already showed meaningful advantages for ATEV over traditional fistulas. Aa a result of meeting the primary superiority endpoint in V012, Humacyte plans to submit a supplemental Biologics License Application (sBLA) to expand the Symvess® label to include a second indication in AV access for hemodialysis in the second half of 2026. For uses other than the FDA approval in the extremity vascular trauma indication, the ATEV is an investigational product and has not been approved for sale by the FDA or any other regulatory agency. About Humacyte Humacyte, Inc. (Nasdaq: HUMA) is developing a disruptive biotechnology platform to deliver universally implantable bioengineered human tissues, advanced tissue constructs, and organ systems designed to improve the lives of patients and transform the practice of medicine. The Company develops and manufactures acellular tissues to treat a wide range of diseases, injuries, and chronic conditions. Humacyte’s Biologics License Application for the acellular tissue engineered vessel (ATEV) in the vascular trauma indication was approved by the FDA in December 2024. ATEVs are also currently in late-stage clinical trials targeting other vascular applications, including arteriovenous (AV) access for hemodialysis and peripheral artery disease (PAD). Preclinical development is also underway in coronary artery bypass grafts, pediatric heart surgery, treatment of type 1 diabetes, and multiple novel cell and tissue applications. Humacyte’s 6mm ATEV for AV access in hemodialysis was the first product candidate to receive the FDA’s Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy (RMAT) designation and has also received FDA Fast Track designation. Humacyte’s 6mm ATEV for urgent arterial repair following extremity vascular trauma and for advanced PAD also have received RMAT designations. The ATEV received priority designation for the treatment of vascular trauma by the U.S. Secretary of Defense. For more information, visit www.Humacyte.com . title: Qassim Cement signs financing agreement for fourth production line
summary: Qassim Cement signs financing agreement for fourth production line
body_text: Saudi Arabia: Qassim Cement has signed an agreement with the Saudi Industrial Development Fund (SIDF) to secure US$105m of funding for the construction of a fourth production line at its plant in the Buraydah region. The funding will help replace certain production lines and boost its capacity to 10,000t/day, according to a stock exchange filing. The financing is for a nine-year period, including a two-year grace period, with a repayment schedule over 7 years. In 2025, Qassim Cement awarded a US$298m contract to China-based Sinoma to set up the fourth cement production line at its Buraydah plant. Under this, Sinoma will provide complete EPC services for the production line.

title: Brex Benchmark: Top 25 Fastest Growing Startups of Summer 2026
summary: This summer's leaderboard belongs to the infrastructure layer — where the majority of customers of a database company is now software.
body_text: Fourteen of the 25 fastest-growing software vendors on Brex this summer — more than half the list — sell infrastructure for building AI products, not AI products themselves. Six more are AI products built on those stacks. Behind #1 Together AI, which rents access to open models, sit the databases, GPUs, caches, and sandboxes that agent products get built on. The last time a Benchmark list looked like this, the products on top were mobile apps and the infrastructure was AWS. The fastest-growing line items on startup card statements are the plumbing of the agent economy, and how startups buy that plumbing shows what they're building. The Summer Benchmark goes deep on the two categories driving the list, AI compute and databases, whose purchase patterns answer questions nobody outside the vendors can measure. When do startups start running open models? Does open compute replace Big Lab bills or grow alongside them? And what happens in the 90 days after a founder prompts an app into existence? The Top 25 Fastest Growing Startups (Summer 2026) These rankings capture growth acceleration and are the companies pulling away right now, not ones already large. Vendors that are publicly traded, valued above $30B, or past $1B in ARR graduate off the list, along with their subsidiaries. The data is real Brex card and Brex bill pay activity from tens of thousands of Brex customers, recency-weighted. The highlighted in the ranking below marks all fourteen as the building blocks for shipping AI products. Ranked by momentum, scaling velocity, and dollar-growth acceleration across 35,000+ Brex customers' card and bill pay activity, recency-weighted. Jan-Jul 2026. Source: Brex data Startups go direct for compute in their first year Everything required to turn those files into a working product is not, and a whole category of vendors now sells that work pre-assembled. What is Together AI actually selling? An open-weight model is free to download: tens to hundreds of gigabytes of numbers that do nothing on their own. Turning them into a product takes GPUs big enough to hold them, an inference engine like vLLM, and a serving layer that batches web requests into efficient GPU work. A whole category now sells that work pre-assembled. GPU clouds rent the raw machines. Serverless platforms like Modal and RunPod add containers, autoscaling, and per-second billing. Then a the top, Together AI, Deepinfra, Baseten, and Fireworks serve popular open models behind compatible endpoints. Change one line of config and the model becomes DeepSeek or Kimi, at whatever price the hosts are currently competing down to. The newest rung, Thinking Machines Lab's Tinker API, sells managed fine-tuning, where you shape an open model to your data without touching a GPU. Every rung sells rented inference with more or less of the stack pre-assembled, from metered API pennies to reserved-machine rent. On Brex the metered layers have by far the most buyers; machine tickets are far larger and far fewer. Vendors shown are summer 2026 Benchmark leaders.Trend 3: A healthcare-interoperability newsletter cracked the top 15. Why rent open compute when you already pay for tokens? An H100 rents for around $3.40 an hour, down from roughly $8 in 2023, and batched well it produces tokens from mid-sized open models for pennies per million. Closed frontier APIs list at up to $5 per million input tokens and $25 to $30 per million output. For the workloads that dominate a token bill (tagging and routing data, extracting structure from documents, speech-to-text, image and video generation), an open model is usually good enough, and the gap runs 5x to 20x. A whole merchant category grew up to arbitrage GPU-hours against token prices. Scope note: card and bill-pay data sees the self-serve layer, not invoiced enterprise GPU contracts. That's a census of what startups do, and startups are where new stacks get chosen. New Startups are moving first to Open Source Models on Compute Platforms After building a PMF AI app with a Big Lab API, the costs can balloon as usage scales. Moving to an OSM hosted in the cloud can cut costs 80% overnight. Companies are adding their first open-compute vendor within 5 months for their first Big Lab API bill, twice as fast as in 2024. Median months from a company's first OpenAl/Anthropic API charge to its first charge at an open-model compute vendor (Together Al, Modal, RunPod, Fal, Groq, Deepinfra, Baseten and peers), by year of first LLM API charge. *2025 cohort has a shorter observation window; its fastest quartile graduated in ~2 months. Brex card + hill pay data, Jan 2021 - Jun 2026. Startups route each workload to the cheapest model that clears its quality bar. Token prices are public list prices, July 2026. Overlap and after-adoption figures: Brex card + bill pay data. Trend 2: The database customer is no longer human Measured within each company's first 12 months on Brex, Supabase adoption grew roughly 17x between the 2022 and 2025 startup cohorts; nearly 1 in 10 companies that joined in 2025 paid for it in their first year. Vendor telemetry explains the new default: Neon, a Postgres company (part of Databricks, ineligible here), reports that AI agents, not people, create more than 80% of its new databases, and Supabase independently reports more than 60% launched by AI tools. The majority customer of a database company is now software. Why do agents need a different kind of database? A classic cloud database couples compute and storage on one machine: minutes to provision, billed while idle, nerve-wracking to copy. The new generation (Neon is the cleanest example) splits it into disposable compute over durable storage built on a replicated log. A new database becomes a seconds-long metadata operation, an idle one suspends to near zero, and a copy is a pointer, not a transfer. Splitting Postgres into disposable compute and durable log-structured storage is what makes instant provisioning, scale-to-zero pricing, and copy-on-write branching possible - the three properties Al agents require. Neon is the cleanest example of the architecture; Supabase, Railway, and peers apply variants of it. None of it was designed for agents; it fits them perfectly. Agents work at machine speed, so a minutes-long provision is a blocking failure. Agents are prolific: a coding agent or app builder like Lovable, Bolt, or Replit provisions a database for each app it generates, thousands a day, most of which sit idle. Near-zero idle cost makes that pattern economically boring instead of absurd, and it's already the norm: Replit's agent runs its backend on Neon, and Retool manages more than 300,000 Postgres instances there with a single engineer. And because the training corpus is saturated with Postgres, LLMs speak it fluently, turning the category's decade-old Postgres bet into an advantage nobody planned. What the buying data shows Our data shows what happens when this machinery meets startups: The default flipped. Among first-ever database purchases, Supabase's share went from about 15% in 2023 to 38% in 2026, the most common first pick. Pinecone, the RAG wave's default entry point, went from 22% to under 2% over the same window. Vector search didn't die; it moved inside Postgres. (We can't see inside consolidated AWS bills; this measures which brands startups pick when choosing a database on its own merits.) The compounding isn't one vendor. The 17x cohort curve that opened this section repeats down the category: Neon's first-year adoption grew about 60x from a tiny base over the same period, and PlanetScale's roughly 5x. The vibe-code funnel is real. Among companies whose first prompt-to-app-builder purchase (Lovable, Replit, or Bolt) came in 2025 or 2026, 9.6% added a paid database within 90 days (more than an order of magnitude above the base rate), and 8.2% chose Supabase or Neon. Among companies that add one, the median gap from first app-builder charge to first Supabase or Neon charge is 106 days: just over a quarter from "prompted an app into existence" to "paying for a production backend." App-builder adopters attach databases at a higher rate than users of professional AI coding tools: net-new demand, and a conversion no single vendor can see. Share of companies' first-ever database-category purchase captured by each vendor, by year of that first purchase. Category spans 20+ modern database and vector database vendors. *2026 is Jan-Jun. Brex card + bill pay data, merchant history to 2021. Source: Brex data Share of active-spending Brex customers that paid each vendor within 12 months of their first Brex spend, by year of first spend. Cohorts restricted to companies with a full 12-month observation window. Brex card + bill pay data, 2021-2026. Source: Brex data Above the entry point sits PlanetScale (#24, the only Postgres company on this summer's list), which brought its locally attached NVMe architecture, Metal, to Postgres last year for the latency-critical case where an agent chains hundreds of queries. It barely shows up in first-year adoption by design: it dropped its free tier years ago and leaves free provisioning to Supabase and Neon. Measurable performance-tier alternatives are flat or shrinking among startups; the rest hides inside consolidated hyperscaler bills, where card data can't see it. Entry-tier bills are flat or falling: the median is tens of dollars a month (Supabase's Pro plan is $25; Neon meters usage with no minimum), and Railway's median bill halved even as its paying customers grew nearly 8x. The revenue engine is count, not contract size: millions of tiny databases created by software, priced like a utility, growing with every app an agent generates. The database industry spent thirty years selling to database administrators. The companies winning the entry point in 2026 sell to other people's software. The infrastructure layer is where the agent race gets funded Spring's trend was abstraction: value accruing to whoever sits in front of a fragmenting market. Summer's trend is what those abstractions run on. Every voice agent, coding agent, and generative media product on this list resolves into the same two purchases, compute to run models and databases to hold state, and startups now make both in their first year, at small dollar amounts, by the tens of thousands. Those two purchases are the earliest reliable signal for which agent-era companies are becoming real businesses. Methodology and privacy Sumeet Marwaha is the Head of Data at Brex, supporting Brex in understanding how customers spend, adopt tools, and grow their businesses. All analysis conducted for this report that uses Brex internal customer data is anonymized and aggregated for privacy. To learn more about how we use data in anonymized or aggregated form for these trend reports, email us at privacy@brex.com.

title: Preventive Maintenance Software for Small Crews (2026): Schedule Board You Own
summary: Build preventive maintenance scheduling software small crews own with Taskade Genesis. Compare against ServiceTitan memberships and spreadsheet PM trackers.
body_text: Blog AI Preventive Maintenance… On this page (19) Taskade Genesis gives small field-service crews a preventive maintenance schedule board, customer equipment history, and renewal reminders linked to daily dispatch, without enterprise membership modules or spreadsheets nobody opens until a contract expires. This guide covers honest PM software choices in 2026. TL;DR: Enterprise field-service suites win complex membership billing and call-center upsells. Spreadsheets win until the first renewal slips. Taskade Genesis wins small crews who want PM schedules sitting beside dispatch in one system they own and reshape. New accounts get a one-time 6,000 credit grant, which is enough to generate the board and look at real fields before paying. Generate a preventive maintenance schedule board → Related: HVAC dispatch board you own , recurring service agreements for field ops , ServiceTitan alternative for small crews . Competitor figures below are publicly listed or widely reported ranges as of July 2026. Vendors change tiers, and ServiceTitan does not publish a list price at all. Confirm live quotes before you sign anything. 🧰 What Small Crews Actually Need From PM Software A full field-service management suite promises memberships, pricebooks, dispatch, marketing attribution, payroll, inventory, and call recording. A five-truck shop lives in a much narrower week: A contract exists, and somebody has to remember it exists. A visit comes due, and the office needs to see it before the customer calls.
